chapters.title: Chapter 58 Yun Wanqing Was Made to Cry by Him
paragraphs: Zhang Xian looked at her resolute expression and continued, "If you don't accept it, I won't do any more business with your Cloud Raiment Pavilion in the future."
Yun Wanqing shook her head. "No, Fellow Daoist. I absolutely will not accept it. Don't try to provoke me like this."
Zhang Xian suddenly smiled. "Then I'll give you something else. If you want it, you have to accept both together."
Yun Wanqing was taken aback. What kind of strange request was this?
"How is Zhen'er doing now?" Zhang Xian abruptly changed the subject.

"She's... she's fine. She's currently staying within the Profound Ice Array," Yun Wanqing answered instinctively before freezing completely. Why was Zhang Xian suddenly asking about this? Could it be—
Zhang Xian didn't speak. He just silently took out a crystal-clear lotus seed from his sleeve and placed it on the table.
Yun Wanqing was utterly shocked. Her beautiful eyes widened, and her voice trembled slightly. "This... this is..."

"The Heaven-Seizing Heart-Mending Lotus Seed. It will be of great use to your daughter," Zhang Xian said softly. "I've looked into it. While it can't completely cure the deficiency in her soul, it can at least improve her condition, enough to spare her from the suffering of the Profound Ice Array."
Yun Wanqing covered her mouth as clear tears slid from the corners of her eyes.
Two hundred years...
She had desperately searched for a way to save her daughter, but to no avail. Now, hope was right before her eyes. She could no longer control her emotions and began sobbing uncontrollably.
Outside the flying vessel.
Su Ling suddenly spoke up. "Zhang Xian made Sect Master Yun cry."
The elders: "???"
Elder Wangya instantly appeared beside Su Ling, his voice rising several octaves, all decorum lost. "What did you say!!?"
Su Ling's face remained calm. "Beneath the protective barrier, I couldn't hear clearly; I could only see a blurry image. Zhang Xian wanted to give her something, and she started crying."
Only then did Wangya let out a sigh of relief, his feelings complex—both happy and distressed.
Yun Wanqing was crying tears of joy; Zhang Xian must have produced something useful for her daughter. The regret was that it wasn't me who provided it.
The other elders nearby also breathed a sigh of relief. Elder Su Ling, please finish your sentences in one go next time! Leaving things half-said is enough to scare someone to death.
Didn't you see Elder Wangya's spiritual power flaring up just now? He almost charged over to attack!
Inside the cabin.

Yun Wanqing reined in her emotions and bowed deeply to Zhang Xian. "Fellow Daoist Zhang Xian, I will remember this kindness and favor in my heart forever. Please tell me what you require; I... this humble one will do my utmost to fulfill it."
[Ding! Current Favorability: 43.]
Looking at her tear-streaked face, Zhang Xian suddenly felt like teasing her. "Didn't you say before that as long as your daughter was cured, you would be willing to pay any price?"
Yun Wanqing instantly panicked, her cheeks flushing slightly red. "Th-this doesn't count as curing my daughter! It... it doesn't count!"
What if he really makes an excessive demand? What should I do?
Zhang Xian laughed. "Then how about agreeing to half?"
"Half?" Yun Wanqing's heart raced as countless possibilities flashed through her mind. She subconsciously took half a step back. "Half of what?"

Seeing her flustered appearance, Zhang Xian finally said, "Oh, my request is simply for you to continue helping me acquire rare treasures and materials—anything and everything. I was very satisfied with the two items Yun Qi gave me last time."
Yun Wanqing let out a sigh of relief, her tense shoulders relaxing. "So that's what it is... I thought... Of course, that's no problem at all."
Right then, she suddenly noticed a mischievous glint flash in Zhang Xian's eyes and realized he had been deliberately teasing her just now!
"You!" Yun Wanqing's cheeks flushed redder with a mix of embarrassment and annoyance. "Fellow Daoist Zhang Xian, is teasing people like this very amusing?"
Zhang Xian laughed heartily. "Sect Master Yun looked much more lively when you were nervous just now compared to usual."
Yun Wanqing glared at him, but for some reason, the heavy feeling that had weighed on her heart for years seemed to lighten a bit because of this jest.
Afterward, she carefully stored away the pill and suddenly noticed that this Immortal Ascension Pill in her hand was slightly different from the one she had given him before.
"This pill..."

Zhang Xian smiled mysteriously. "Our minor world has already deciphered the recipe for the Immortal Ascension Pill. This one is an improved version. It's somewhat different from the ones refined by the Lingxu Sect; this one is more effective. By the way, you absolutely cannot give this one away! You must take it yourself."
"I will definitely take it myself."
Yun Wanqing was utterly shocked in her heart. She finally realized that the young man before her likely represented a force far beyond what the Cloud Raiment Pavilion could imagine.
So it wasn't that we were cooperating; Cloud Raiment Pavilion had latched onto a powerful patron!
One hour later, the flying vessel's protective barrier was finally lifted. Yun Wanqing summoned Zhiyin from Heavenly Puppet Peak to handle the handover of the vessel matters.
"Come collect it in one month," Zhiyin said to Zhang Xian with a wink. "I guarantee Boss will be satisfied then.

Subsequently, Elder Wangya forced himself to maintain his composure as he came to see them off. Yun Wanqing was clearly somewhat distracted; after hurriedly bidding farewell, she departed on her vessel, eager to rush back and treat her daughter.
Looking back at the gradually receding Yunmiao Sect, Yun Wanqing's thoughts were in turmoil. This trip was originally intended to repay a favor, yet she ended up owing an even greater one.
"Agreeing to half..." A slight smile touched the corner of her mouth.
Spirit Sword Peak, in front of Zhang Xian's thatched hut.

Li Fuxi sat with eyes closed, cultivating her qi. After consuming the many rare treasures and materials given by Zhang Xian and secluding herself for a month in meditation, her Metal and Water Spirit Roots had both advanced from high-grade to top-grade.

Simultaneously, she steeled herself and shattered her originally damaged Golden Core before re-condensing a new one. She had now reached the second layer of the Golden Core stage. The entire person seemed reborn from nirvana-like flames. Although her cultivation level was lower now, her foundation was several times more solid than in the past.

On the other side of the thatched hut, Zhenhai, Chen Tiexin, and Lin Yinyin sat on stone stools. Zhenhai and Chen Tiexin were exchanging glances frantically with their eyes, while Lin Yinyin pouted slightly, staring blankly at the flying vessel in mid-air.
Only after Yun Wanqing left did Zhang Xian jump down from mid-air. Seeing his master and fellow disciples all waiting for him, he greeted them each in turn.

Li Fuxi swept her gaze over Zhang Xian and said indifferently, "Giving you a flying vessel and treating you as an equal... It seems I still underestimated you." She then called over Lin Yinyin, who was sulking off to the side. "Yinyin, let's go."
"Hmph!" This time Lin Yinyin surprisingly obeyed her master so readily. She jumped onto her master's flying sword, and with a whoosh sound, the two flew back to the mountaintop.
Huh? Did they stay behind just to look down on me? Zhang Xian unconsciously rubbed his nose.
"Quick! Quick! Tell your Senior Brother what exactly happened!"
"I need firsthand information! The entire sect is probably going crazy today." Chen Tiexin had already activated his recording talisman.
Zhang Xian: "..."
Atop Spirit Sword Peak, the night breeze was slightly cool.
Lin Yinyin followed behind Li Fuxi, her little face puffed up like a steamed bun. As soon as they entered the thatched hut, she plopped down onto a meditation cushion.
"Master! I don't want to cultivate the Nine Turns Jade Condensation Sutra anymore!"
Li Fuxi frowned slightly. "Nonsense! Absolutely not!"

"If I keep cultivating it any longer, Brother Zhang Xian is going to be snatched away by someone else!" Lin Yinyin tugged at her master's sleeve aggrievedly. "First there was Liu Qingxuan, now there's Yun Wanqing... I'm so pitiful."
Li Fuxi sighed inwardly.
That kid Zhang Xian might be average-looking and have poor aptitude, but he truly is frighteningly wealthy. Even I owe him an enormous favor, not knowing how I can ever repay him.

chapters.title: Chapter 59 Let’s Team Up and Drain Him Dry
paragraphs: Seeing the sorrow etched on her disciple’s face, Li Fuxi sighed helplessly. "You must focus on your cultivation. At the very least, achieve some success in forming your Golden Core. Then, this Master will no longer forbid you from... dual cultivating with him. By then, it would count as a minor accomplishment in the Nine Turns Jade Condensation Sutra."
She paused briefly before adding in a hushed tone, "And even if true dual cultivation isn't immediately possible... you can still be with him..."
Her words caught in her throat. A specific memory flashed through her mind—the scene she had inadvertently witnessed with her divine sense back at the spirit spring.
Ah! How could they be so shameless?
Two patches of crimson bloomed on Li Fuxi’s jade-white cheeks.
"Be with him... doing what?" Lin Yinyin asked innocently.
Li Fuxi struggled to articulate her thoughts. After a long silence, she finally squeezed out a vague reply. "...In short... you have methods to keep him tied to you."

"Ah!" Seeing the mix of embarrassment and indignation on Li Fuxi’s face, realization dawned on Lin Yinyin. A blush instantly spread from the roots of her ears down to her neck. "Master... You saw us..."

"No! This Master saw absolutely nothing!" Li Fuxi snapped, forcing a mask of composure. "It is getting late. Go meditate for a while. Shortly, I will assist you in unblocking your meridians again so you can reach the late Foundation Establishment stage as soon as possible."
Lin Yinyin cleared her throat lightly to banish the awkwardness and produced a small white jade bottle from within her robes. "There is no need to trouble Master for that. I have a faster method."
"This is..."
"A treasure Brother Zhang Xian gave me!" Lin Yinyin declared, shaking her little head triumphantly. "Master, come with me."

Lin Yinyin darted over to the edge of the spirit spring with practiced ease. She arranged three water spirit stones and two metal spirit stones, then carefully poured a single drop of spiritual liquid from the jade bottle into the water.
In a split second, the murky spring water turned crystal clear, revealing the bottom. Simultaneously, the spiritual energy grew so dense it transformed into a mist, rolling off the water’s surface.

Li Fuxi was inwardly alarmed. Enhancing a spirit spring with five mid-grade spirit stones? Even she would hesitate to spend so extravagantly! And although she didn't recognize the liquid in the bottle, judging by the extraordinary reaction of the spring, it was undoubtedly a rare treasure.
"Master, hurry up!" Lin Yinyin had already nimbly stripped off her outer garments and slipped into the water like a little fish.
Li Fuxi walked to the water's edge but hesitated. She stepped into the shallows but felt too self-conscious to remove her robes.
"It needs to touch the skin directly to be effective!" Lin Yinyin suddenly swam over, her wet little hands grabbing her Master’s sash.
"Wait! Yinyin, don't—"
Splash!

Li Fuxi’s plain white Daoist robe drifted onto the water’s surface. The moonlight caressed the woman’s jade-like skin, water droplets sliding along her exquisite collarbones before disappearing into the deep, proud valley of her cleavage.
"Wow!" Lin Yinyin’s eyes went wide and round.
Envy!
Whoosh!
Li Fuxi submerged herself completely, leaving only a pair of large, indignant eyes above the surface. Her voice came out muffled through the water. "Y-you rebellious disciple!

However, as the spiritual energy within the spring frantically surged into her meridians, Li Fuxi couldn't help but let out a soft, contented moan. This sensation of being gently swaddled in pure spiritual power was indeed addictive.
Yinyin had not lied. Cultivating in this manner was indeed several times faster than usual.
Such a luxurious cultivation method... Li Fuxi realized that looking across the entire Southern Region, almost no one could enjoy such extravagance.
"Zhang Xian treats you really well," she murmured subconsciously.

Lin Yinyin suddenly wilted. "But Brother treats everyone so well. That Pavilion Master Yun must have received many benefits from him; otherwise, why would she personally come to our door? And Chief Liu is constantly trying to matchmake his daughter with him; even I've heard the rumors."
Suddenly leaning closer, she blinked her big eyes mischievously. "Oh right, Master, what did Brother say to you privately that day? He wouldn't tell me!"
"N-nothing!" Li Fuxi shrank back entirely. "He merely advised this Master not to enter secluded meditation for life-or-death breakthroughs... I thought about it and... it made some sense."
"What? That's letting him off too easy! Next time I'll help Master get something from him. Brother is really rich."
"N-no, that's not appropriate... What kind of Master asks her disciple for things?" Li Fuxi’s voice lacked conviction.
"Master, you can't think like that! If we don't ask for things, they'll all just end up benefiting other little vixens!"
Lin Yinyin gnashed her teeth and slapped the water's surface. "Master, we're family! Let's team up and drain him dry!"
Li Fuxi: "..."

After watching Lin Yinyin play around for a while, Li Fuxi closed her eyes and focused her mind within the spirit spring. As her energy circulated through its cycles, feeling the flow of power within her body, Li Fuxi's inner astonishment grew even greater.

The efficacy of this spiritual liquid far exceeded her expectations. Not only did it increase the speed of spiritual energy circulation several times over, but even more remarkably, it contained a trace of Heavenly Dao charm, allowing her understanding of her cultivation technique to deepen by several degrees.

After completing one full cycle of energy circulation, Li Fuxi slowly opened her eyes. Through the clear spring water, she saw Lin Yinyin resting her chin in her hands, blinking her big eyes as she stared straight at her.
Master was always so fierce before... Why does she look kind of cute when she's quiet?
Li Fuxi felt somewhat self-conscious under her disciple's direct gaze and turned her face slightly away. "Yinyin, why are you staring at this Master?"
Lin Yinyin giggled and moved closer. "Master is really beautiful."
Li Fuxi was taken aback for a moment before letting out a light hmph. "Nonsense."
Lin Yinyin's eyes rolled thoughtfully before she suddenly sighed with regret. "It's a pity this bottle of Dragon Saliva Jade Liquid has to be returned to Brother Zhang Xian in a few days."
Li Fuxi was slightly startled; her gaze unconsciously fell on the jade bottle in Lin Yinyin's hand.
She sighed inwardly. With the aid of this spiritual liquid, both hers and Lin Yinyin's cultivation speed could increase at least threefold.

Especially since she was currently at a critical stage—shattering and reforming her core. If she could continue using this liquid consistently, she was confident she could return to peak condition within a year... perhaps even advance further.
What a pity...
Such divine objects were bound to be exceptionally precious. The fact that Zhang Xian could lend it to Yinyin was already an enormous favor; how could one dare hope for more?
Lin Yinyin secretly observed her Master's expression; seeing a flicker of regret flash in Li Fuxi's eyes made Lin Yinyin secretly delighted.
She deliberately sighed with feigned melancholy. "Sigh... I'll go beg Brother Zhang Xian later and ask him to lend it for a few more days."
Li Fuxi gently tapped her forehead. "Greedy girl! Being able to borrow such a treasure is already rare enough; don't push your luck."
"But..." Lin Yinyin blinked with an aggrieved expression. "...doesn't Master need it too?"
Li Fuxi was momentarily speechless before stiffening her expression. "That is none of your concern."

Lin Yinyin nodded obediently and said no more, focusing on cultivating peacefully within the spirit spring. Perhaps stimulated by the events of the day, she cultivated with exceptional seriousness throughout the night.
Just before dawn.

The spiritual energy around Lin Yinyin began to fluctuate violently; the spiritual mist in the spring water converged frantically toward her. Her body trembled slightly in the water, and an azure-blue spiritual pattern appeared between her eyebrows.
With a soft pop, the shackles within her body shattered, and an aura belonging to the Foundation Establishment Seventh Layer instantly spread out.
"Master! I succeeded!" The young girl excitedly threw herself into Li Fuxi's embrace.
Li Fuxi showed a rare, approving smile. "Not bad, but what comes next is key."

She gathered a point of spiritual light at her fingertip and lightly tapped Lin Yinyin between the eyebrows. "Next, you need to cultivate your Nine Turns Jade Condensation Sutra until you achieve minor success. You possess a top-grade Water Spirit Root; now you can begin preparing to condense your Golden Core."
"The grade of a Golden Core, much like magical treasures, is divided into five ranks: Heaven, Earth, Mysterious, Yellow, and White."

"The first rank: White Grade Golden Core. The core body is dull and lacks luster; no phenomena occur during its formation. Spiritual power reserves are almost identical to peak Foundation Establishment, and the improvement in combat power is limited."
"The second rank: Yellow Grade Golden Core. The surface possesses a faint spiritual light; this belongs to the average standard."

"The third rank: Mysterious Grade Golden Core. The core appears a mixed blue-purple. Not many cultivators achieve this grade; those who do are already considered outstanding talents within the cultivation world."

"The fourth rank: Earth Grade Golden Core. The core interweaves crimson and gold. This is typically formed by direct disciples of top-tier sects or those born with Dao bodies. I possess dual spirit roots; by chance, I formed an Earth Grade Golden Core. But my expectations for you go beyond this."

Li Fuxi's expression turned solemn. "What I want to talk about is the fifth rank: The Heaven Grade Golden Core! The entire core resembles colored glaze. Legends say when such cores form, auspicious clouds descend from the heavens, and purple qi rolls in from the east, spanning thousands of miles. It is said only the Yunmiao Sect’s founding patriarch ever condensed such a Golden Core."

"Starting from the Earth Grade Golden Core and upward, tribulation lightning inevitably consists of six layers. This is also why this Master insists you cultivate the Nine Turns Jade Condensation Sutra—even achieving only minor success can ensure your fleshly body becomes like jade, impervious to myriad techniques. During your tribulation crossing, you will have greater assurance."
Listening attentively to Li Fuxi’s earnest teachings, Lin Yinyin’s beautiful eyes sparkled continuously.
Just a few years ago, she was merely a little girl at the Qi Refining stage... In just these few short years, she had already touched the threshold leading toward Golden Core formation.

"Next, you need to cultivate your Nine Turns Jade Condensation Sutra until you achieve minor success.
You possess a top-grade Water Spirit Root; now you can begin preparing to condense your Golden Core."
"The grade of a Golden Core, much like magical treasures, is divided into five ranks: Heaven, Earth, Mysterious, Yellow, and White."
"The first rank: White Grade Golden Core.
The core body is dull and lacks luster; no phenomena occur during its formation.
Spiritual power reserves are almost identical to peak Foundation Establishment, and the improvement in combat power is limited."
"The second rank: Yellow Grade Golden Core.
The surface possesses a faint spiritual light; this belongs to the average standard."
"The third rank: Mysterious Grade Golden Core.
The core appears a mixed blue-purple.
Not many cultivators achieve this grade; those who do are already considered outstanding talents within the cultivation world."
"The fourth rank: Earth Grade Golden Core.
The core interweaves crimson and gold.
This is typically formed by direct disciples of top-tier sects or those born with Dao bodies.
I possess dual spirit roots; by chance, I formed an Earth Grade Golden Core.
But my expectations for you go beyond this."
Li Fuxi's expression turned solemn.
"What I want to talk about is the fifth rank: The Heaven Grade Golden Core!
The entire core resembles colored glaze.
Legends say when such cores form, auspicious clouds descend from the heavens, and purple qi rolls in from the east, spanning thousands of miles.
It is said only the Yunmiao Sect’s founding patriarch ever condensed such a Golden Core."
"Starting from the Earth Grade Golden Core and upward, tribulation lightning inevitably consists of six layers.

This is also why this Master insists you cultivate the Nine Turns Jade Condensation Sutra—even achieving only minor success can ensure your fleshly body becomes like jade, impervious to myriad techniques.
During your tribulation crossing, you will have greater assurance."
Listening attentively to Li Fuxi’s earnest teachings, Lin Yinyin’s beautiful eyes sparkled continuously.
Just a few years ago, she was merely a little girl at the Qi Refining stage...
In just these few short years, she had already touched the threshold leading toward Golden Core formation.

chapters.title: Chapter 60 You Wouldn’t Want Others to Know, Would You
paragraphs: Several more days passed in this manner. Zhang Xian was in his thatched hut, wholly absorbed in studying the art of puppetry. His desk was piled high with various precious materials.

Frowning, he calculated, "One piece of Heavenly Puppet Wood, five pieces of Profound Iron Essence, Spirit Pattern Jade, and Clear Lotus Silk..." As he tallied it up, he couldn't help but sigh. "Twenty thousand sect contribution points are nowhere near enough. Looks like I'll have to buy some more from Senior Sister Tiexin."
Just then, his communication jade slip suddenly lit up. Liu Qingxuan's gentle voice came through. "Zhang Xian, why haven't you been attending classes lately?"

Zhang Xian replied with sincere earnestness, "Supervisor Liu, I've had a premonition these past few days that I'm about to break through to the sixth level of Foundation Establishment. I've been in secluded cultivation."
"I see." Liu Qingxuan's voice carried a note of concern. "Well, you must work hard. If you need any help, just say the word."
No sooner had the call ended than another message arrived, this time from Zhiyin of Heavenly Puppet Peak. "Zhang Xian, do you still have enough materials for making puppets?"
"Not really. I've almost run out of contribution points," Zhang Xian answered with a bitter laugh. "I plan to earn some more sect contribution points and then buy some more."
There was a moment of silence on the other end before the voice spoke again. "Actually, you could also trade with me directly using spirit stones."
"That's allowed?" Zhang Xian asked in surprise. "Doesn't the sect forbid private transactions?"
"In principle, it's not allowed."

"But it's fine if we change our identities. I'm a nominal patron of the Cloud Raiment Pavilion, and you are a distinguished guest of the Cloud Raiment Pavilion. We can trade using spirit stones, and I can even give you a twenty percent discount as a VIP. This is normal business dealings; it has nothing to do with the Yunmiao Sect's rules."
Zhang Xian: "..."
You're something else.
"That's fantastic! Sister, please get me one million spirit stones' worth of materials first. I want the very best."
And so, he continued burying himself in diligent cultivation. When skill falls short, spirit stones make up the difference.
In the evening, Lin Yinyin's message suddenly arrived. "Brother, I have a surprise for you!"
"What surprise?" Zhang Xian asked curiously.
"Just wait and see!"
A short while later, Lin Yinyin arrived riding her sword. She pushed the door open furtively, her little face flushed pink. "Brother, I've missed you so much."
"What about Master?" Zhang Xian asked.
"Hmph! Asking about Master as soon as we meet," Lin Yinyin pretended to be angry before giggling again. "Brother, I came to soak in the spirit spring with you."

Zhang Xian coughed twice and said seriously, "Yinyin, Master also said that your Nine Turns Jade Condensation Sutra is at a critical stage right now. You mustn't slack off and waste all your previous effort."
"Pah! Brother, your own thoughts are wandering," Lin Yinyin covered her mouth and laughed. As she spoke, she pulled Zhang Xian to the hot spring behind the house.
Then she skillfully inserted two wood spirit stones and two water spirit stones into the formation node on the stone wall, along with one metal spirit stone and a drop of Dragon Saliva Jade Liquid.
Zhang Xian was full of question marks. We don't have a metal spiritual root here; why are you adding a metal-attribute spirit stone?
Before he could ask, Lin Yinyin handed him the jade vial. "Here, this is for you."
"Didn't we agree this was a gift for you? Why are you giving it back?" Zhang Xian was even more confused.
Lin Yinyin said earnestly, "Brother, I know this is very precious, but you can't just keep lending it to me forever. From now on, let's soak in the same spirit spring together to avoid waste."
Waste?
Zhang Xian indicated he didn't even know how to write the word 'waste'.
Lin Yinyin's eyes darted around as she proposed another idea. "Having just two people in the spirit spring is still wasteful. How about I call Master over too?"
"What?" Before Zhang Xian could react, Lin Yinyin had already sent the message.

At that moment, atop Spirit Sword Peak, Li Fuxi was meditating when she suddenly received Lin Yinyin's message: "Master! Come quickly to Brother's place to soak in the spirit spring! I've already prepared it!"
Li Fuxi frowned and replied: "Nonsense! How utterly improper!"

"Master! The spirit liquid is so precious; what a pity it would be to waste it!" Lin Yinyin wheedled. "I'll use a Water Mirror Technique to separate Brother from us; we'll each soak on our own side; I guarantee he won't be able to see anything!"
Li Fuxi: "..."
After much hesitation, Li Fuxi decided to go take a look anyway. Seeing the two already waiting by the spirit spring's edge, she said sternly with a stiff face, "What kind of spectacle is this!"

Zhang Xian hurriedly explained, "Master... perhaps it would be better if you and Yinyin went back to soak in one pool together? I'll soak here by myself; at most I'll just use a few more spirit stones and spirit liquid."
"No!" Li Fuxi said severely. "The spirit liquid is far too precious; how can we waste it so casually! You two cultivate here properly; your master will take her leave first."
"Aiya!" Lin Yinyin immediately hugged Li Fuxi's arm. "Right now we can't even absorb all this spiritual energy! Master, let's do it together; otherwise, it really would be wasteful."

Seeing Li Fuxi pause in her steps, Lin Yinyin added, "Don't worry, Master! It's absolutely safe!" As she spoke, she immediately cast a Water Mirror Technique right in the middle of the spring water, splitting the spirit spring into two halves and isolating Zhang Xian on the other side.
Li Fuxi bit her lip, wrestling with herself for a moment before finally being unable to resist the temptation of the spirit spring any longer. She gave a cold nod. "Just this once."
With that said, she waved her hand and added an even sturdier water mirror barrier. Then she slowly loosened her outer robe and stepped into the water along with Lin Yinyin.
In the Spirit Spring.
The Water Mirror Technique blocked their view from each other's side.
But faint rustling sounds of clothing being removed and soft sounds of water gently moving still clearly reached Zhang Xian's ears.
Zhang Xian took a deep breath and silently recited his Heart-Calming Mantra.
On the other side...
Lin Yinyin whispered, "Master... from now on... shall we soak in the spirit spring together like this?"
Li Fuxi had half-submerged herself in the water but still revealed her large eyes above its surface; her ear tips were slightly red. "N-no... this is far too improper..."
"Then... how about next time Brother and I go soak at your place behind your house?" Lin Yinyin pretended not to hear her objection and continued proposing ideas.
Li Fuxi hesitated for what felt like an eternity before finally letting out a muffled "...Mmm..."
There was no helping it—she needed this spirit spring too much.
"Mmm... but going to Master's place might not be good either... what if we get discovered? Wouldn't that be bad? Master, your cultivation is higher; better if you come over here instead..."
She leaned close to Li Fuxi's ear and lowered her voice even further: "...Master... you wouldn't want others to know about us soaking in this spirit spring together... would you?"
Li Fuxi's mind went blank for an instant; she instinctively replied, "...That works too... I'll come over..."
Zhang Xian: "..."
Each of them harbored their own thoughts as they silently cultivated through the night.
The next morning...
Li Fuxi grabbed Lin Yinyin by her collar and hauled her up with an icy expression. "Go attend morning classes at Cloud-Piercing Peak!"
Lin Yinyin was dragged away looking utterly aggrieved but still managed to wink at Zhang Xian before leaving.
At noon...
Zhang Xian received another message from Lin Yinyin:
"So? Was it surprising or not?"
Zhang Xian replied helplessly:
"Nonsense..."
Lin Yinyin sent back:
"Hmph! Not interested? Then next time I won't invite Master over..."
Zhang Xian thought for a moment before replying:
"...Come on over..."
He swore—he was only doing this for Master's sake so she could raise her realm faster—absolutely no other thoughts whatsoever.
Nighttime...
"Master, come quickly~"
Li Fuxi slipped over under the moonlight towards Zhang Xian’s spirit spring location.
The next night...
"Come quickly~"
And again the next day...
"Come~"
And so passed one month...
"Cough..."
By now, Li Fuxi had long since become familiar with the routine—but when she arrived at the spirit spring location today—she found only Lin Yinyin alone there waiting...
"Where’s Zhang Xian?"
Lin Yinyin slapped the water idly, looking bored.
"Hah! He went during the daytime today—got the flying boat from Zhiyin Sister—asked for leave to return to his hometown."

chapters.title: Chapter 61 You Wish
paragraphs: Early that morning, the moment Zhang Xian received the message from Zhiyin, he rushed over without delay.

Upon his arrival at Heavenly Puppet Peak, he found Zhiyin already waiting for him at the summit. She led him into a pocket dimension where a massive flying vessel rested in silence. Small puppets scurried across its surface, performing the final finishing touches.

Zhiyin clapped her hands. From the deck of the vessel, a female cultivator dressed in a form-fitting black robe descended slowly. She possessed a voluptuous, curvaceous figure and a face that bore a seventy percent resemblance to Zhiyin, though her features carried a more heroic, sharper air.

"This is the captain, an early-stage Golden Core puppet," Zhiyin introduced. "You only need to control her; she, in turn, commands the thirty other puppets on board to operate the vessel. However, due to core restrictions, the captain cannot leave the vessel’s immediate vicinity."
Zhang Xian examined her closely. Zhiyin’s craftsmanship was so exquisite that he couldn't find a single flaw to suggest she wasn't human.
"Give her a name," Zhiyin said with a smile.
Zhang Xian thought for a moment. "Let’s call her Yunshang, since this vessel is essentially a gift from Cloud Raiment Pavilion."
The female cultivator bowed slightly, her voice cool and clear. "Thank you, Master, for bestowing this name."
Zhiyin then produced a green jade talisman from her sleeve. "This is the vessel talisman. Once refined, you can summon the ship at any time."

Zhang Xian took the talisman, dripped a drop of essence blood onto it, and began the refinement process. Once finished, a sweep of his divine sense brought a complete, three-dimensional map of the vessel into his mind.
Zhiyin smiled warmly. "A vessel this large might be inconvenient to transport. If you need it, I can sell you a storage item at a dis—"
Before she could finish, the enormous vessel vanished into thin air, tucked away safely in Zhang Xian’s system space.
"Sister Zhiyin, what were you saying just now?"

Zhiyin’s eyes widened in shock. She eventually chuckled softly. "You truly are remarkable. A storage space capable of holding something this massive... few in the Southern Region possess such a thing."
Zhang Xian offered a mysterious smile and cupped his hands. "Thank you for your hard work, Sister Zhiyin. I'll see you another day."
With the vessel secured, Zhang Xian prepared to return to his home world. By his reckoning, it had been a full year since his last visit.
As an inner sect disciple, he didn't require formal permission to leave; a simple registration at the gates sufficed.
"Spirit Sword Peak, Zhang Xian. Returning home to visit family. Expected return in two months."
After registering, Zhang Xian stepped past the sect gates. It was noon, and the area was bustling with disciples. Suddenly, Zhang Xian summoned the massive vessel out of thin air.
The onlookers were left dumbfounded as Zhang Xian waved casually and leaped onto the deck.
"Holy crap!" one of the gate guards exclaimed.
"Is that the rich guy? He’s taking a flying vessel just to visit family?"
"Damn, this guy is too showy."
"I heard the fuel for one day on that thing costs 800 sect points," another whispered. "That’s five years of gate duty for us!"
"Stop talking about it. Comparing yourself to him just makes life feel worse."
Zhang Xian stood at the bow, feeling the wind rush against his face.
"Yunshang, set course for Shuiyun City."
"As you command, Master."
The vessel ascended, its internal formations humming to life. It accelerated like an arrow released from a bowstring, shooting toward the clouds.

Zhang Xian explored the interior. The study was filled with classic texts, the cultivation chambers were embedded with spirit-gathering arrays, and the tearoom was fully furnished. There were over ten bedrooms, and to his delight, a hot spring pool filled with crystal-clear, spirit-rich water.
"Master, would you like me to prepare food?" a maid puppet asked respectfully.
Zhang Xian waved a hand. "No need. I’ll soak for a while."
As he relaxed in the warm water, a maid puppet knelt by the poolside, offering spirit fruits and tea.
This is the true immortal life, Zhang Xian thought. He realized he had been far too frugal in the past.
The only downside was the reading material. The study held only "classics." There were none of the popular novels currently trending in the Yunmiao Sect.

Then again, those novels were usually about underdogs rising against the odds. As a second-generation immortal heir, Zhang Xian knew he’d be the villain who wouldn't survive ten chapters in those stories.
Seven days later, Shuiyun City appeared on the horizon.
Looking down at the familiar cityscape, Zhang Xian felt little. With the Zhao family gone, nothing here held his concern.
With a thought, he stored the vessel and arrived at a hidden valley on the outskirts. Amidst the overgrown weeds, a weak, white spatial vortex rotated slowly—the entrance to the Daliang small world.
Passing through the rift, the thin atmosphere immediately made him uncomfortable. This world lacked spiritual energy entirely.

He summoned the vessel once more and headed toward Xuanwei’s temple. As the bamboo grove came into view, he was surprised to see a faint cyan light shield enveloping the grounds. A protective formation was operating at full capacity.
"Something happened.
His heart tightened. He leapt from the vessel, dropping a hundred zhang through the air.
The moment his feet touched the ground, a sharp sword light stabbed toward him.
"It’s me!" Zhang Xian shouted, releasing his aura to signal his identity.
The sword stopped abruptly. Li Miaoyin appeared in the courtyard, looking utterly exhausted. Her Foundation Establishment second-stage cultivation seemed dangerously unstable.
"Lord Guardian Duke?" she exclaimed, her face lighting up with joy.
Zhang Xian spread his divine sense. The temple was in ruins. Aside from Li Miaoyin, he could only sense the weak life signs of Xuanwei and Yu Yun. No one else remained.
"What happened here?"
Li Miaoyin’s expression darkened. She beckoned him into a bedroom where the thick scent of medicinal herbs hung in the air.

Elder Daoist Xuanwei lay weakly in bed, having reverted to his aged appearance. Even more alarming was Yu Yun. Her face was as pale as paper, her breath flickering like a candle in the wind, surrounded by life-sustaining arrays.
"Who did this?" Zhang Xian’s voice turned icy cold.
Xuanwei replied hoarsely, "It’s alright... the enemies were dealt with by Yu Yun."

Li Miaoyin’s voice trembled as she explained. "Three months ago, a Foundation Establishment cultivator and two Qi Refining disciples appeared. They claimed to be from the Muling Sect, visiting while training in this small world."
"We entertained them, but they suddenly attacked. They injured us and began slaughtering the other disciples."

"We survived only because of our magic treasures," Li Miaoyin continued, a glint of fear in her eyes. "Yu Yun risked everything. She used spirit talismans and was even willing to self-detonate her artifacts to hold them off."
"We managed to kill two of them, but one Qi Refining disciple had a powerful escape technique and got away."
She looked at Yu Yun with heartache. "Yu Yun blew up five spirit talismans to kill their leader. But her meridians are damaged... her future cultivation path is likely over."
Yu Yun forced a weak smile, blood staining the corners of her mouth. "I refine those talismans every day for this reason. I never thought they'd actually be used."
"When fighting, you must be fast, accurate, and ruthless," Yu Yun said proudly. "I learned that from you."
She coughed violently, spitting up fresh blood.
"No regrets," Yu Yun whispered. "A Qi Refining stage cultivator killing a Foundation Establishment master... I've earned it. It's time for me to go accompany Shijie down below anyway."
Zhang Xian looked at her and growled, "You wish!"

"Yunshang, set course for Shuiyun City."
"As you command, Master."
The vessel ascended, its internal formations humming to life.
It accelerated like an arrow released from a bowstring, shooting toward the clouds.
Zhang Xian explored the interior.
The study was filled with classic texts, the cultivation chambers were embedded with spirit-gathering arrays, and the tearoom was fully furnished.
There were over ten bedrooms, and to his delight, a hot spring pool filled with crystal-clear, spirit-rich water.
"Master, would you like me to prepare food?" a maid puppet asked respectfully.
Zhang Xian waved a hand.
"No need.
I’ll soak for a while."
As he relaxed in the warm water, a maid puppet knelt by the poolside, offering spirit fruits and tea.
This is the true immortal life, Zhang Xian thought.
He realized he had been far too frugal in the past.
The only downside was the reading material.
The study held only "classics." There were none of the popular novels currently trending in the Yunmiao Sect.
Then again, those novels were usually about underdogs rising against the odds.
As a second-generation immortal heir, Zhang Xian knew he’d be the villain who wouldn't survive ten chapters in those stories.
Seven days later, Shuiyun City appeared on the horizon.
Looking down at the familiar cityscape, Zhang Xian felt little.
With the Zhao family gone, nothing here held his concern.
With a thought, he stored the vessel and arrived at a hidden valley on the outskirts.
Amidst the overgrown weeds, a weak, white spatial vortex rotated slowly—the entrance to the Daliang small world.
Passing through the rift, the thin atmosphere immediately made him uncomfortable.
This world lacked spiritual energy entirely.
He summoned the vessel once more and headed toward Xuanwei’s temple.
As the bamboo grove came into view, he was surprised to see a faint cyan light shield enveloping the grounds.
A protective formation was operating at full capacity.
"Something happened.
His heart tightened.
He leapt from the vessel, dropping a hundred zhang through the air.
The moment his feet touched the ground, a sharp sword light stabbed toward him.
"It’s me!" Zhang Xian shouted, releasing his aura to signal his identity.
The sword stopped abruptly.
Li Miaoyin appeared in the courtyard, looking utterly exhausted.
Her Foundation Establishment second-stage cultivation seemed dangerously unstable.
"Lord Guardian Duke?" she exclaimed, her face lighting up with joy.
Zhang Xian spread his divine sense.
The temple was in ruins.
Aside from Li Miaoyin, he could only sense the weak life signs of Xuanwei and Yu Yun.
No one else remained.
"What happened here?"
Li Miaoyin’s expression darkened.
She beckoned him into a bedroom where the thick scent of medicinal herbs hung in the air.
Elder Daoist Xuanwei lay weakly in bed, having reverted to his aged appearance.
Even more alarming was Yu Yun.
Her face was as pale as paper, her breath flickering like a candle in the wind, surrounded by life-sustaining arrays.
"Who did this?" Zhang Xian’s voice turned icy cold.
Xuanwei replied hoarsely, "It’s alright... the enemies were dealt with by Yu Yun."
Li Miaoyin’s voice trembled as she explained.
"Three months ago, a Foundation Establishment cultivator and two Qi Refining disciples appeared.
They claimed to be from the Muling Sect, visiting while training in this small world."
"We entertained them, but they suddenly attacked.
They injured us and began slaughtering the other disciples."
"We survived only because of our magic treasures," Li Miaoyin continued, a glint of fear in her eyes.
"Yu Yun risked everything.
She used spirit talismans and was even willing to self-detonate her artifacts to hold them off."
"We managed to kill two of them, but one Qi Refining disciple had a powerful escape technique and got away."
She looked at Yu Yun with heartache.
"Yu Yun blew up five spirit talismans to kill their leader.
But her meridians are damaged... her future cultivation path is likely over."
Yu Yun forced a weak smile, blood staining the corners of her mouth.
"I refine those talismans every day for this reason.
I never thought they'd actually be used."
"When fighting, you must be fast, accurate, and ruthless," Yu Yun said proudly.
"I learned that from you."
She coughed violently, spitting up fresh blood.
"No regrets," Yu Yun whispered.
"A Qi Refining stage cultivator killing a Foundation Establishment master...
I've earned it.
It's time for me to go accompany Shijie down below anyway."
Zhang Xian looked at her and growled, "You wish!"

chapters.title: Chapter 62 Maybe They’re Just as Lustful as You
paragraphs: After Zhang Xian finished speaking, Li Miaoyin and Xuanwei, who were standing nearby, wore expressions of mild displeasure.
"Hah," Yu Yun let out a self-mocking laugh. "I’m already a dying man. I’m not afraid of you."
"Wanting to die isn't that easy," Zhang Xian countered.

He walked to Yu Yun's bedside. With a series of crisp thuds, he produced a row of jade boxes: Heart-Seizing Heaven-Mending Lotus Seeds, Immortal Ascension Grass, Immortal Ascension Pills, and Marrow Cleansing Fruits.
Although the others couldn't identify the treasures, a rich, ancient herbal fragrance instantly filled the room. It was clear at a glance that these were no ordinary goods.
"This is..." Li Miaoyin was stunned.
"Come on, everyone gets a share." Zhang Xian beckoned them over and began distributing the items.
[Ding! Gifted to Li Miaoyin]
Several days later, under the restorative power of the pills, Xuanwei regained his youthful appearance. Yu Yun was not only able to get out of bed but could walk with ease.

Beyond that, each of them experienced a profound evolution in their Spirit Roots. Xuanwei and Yu Yun reached High-Grade status, while Li Miaoyin—the most talented of the group—achieved a Supreme Spirit Root.
"The Duke is becoming increasingly unfathomable," Xuanwei sighed, gazing up at the massive flying vessel hovering in the sky.
"Treasures that enhance Spirit Roots are worth a fortune," Li Miaoyin added. "Yet to him, they seem as common as cabbages. It’s simply unbelievable."

Sitting in his wheelchair, Yu Yun felt a pang of regret. It was unclear whether he was sad he couldn't "join his senior sister" in the afterlife or simply overwhelmed by yet another massive favor from Zhang Xian.
Zhang Xian descended from the vessel. Over the past few days, he had patrolled nearly the entire small world without detecting further intruders.
"Tell me about those Muling Sect disciples," Zhang Xian said, turning to the details of the attack.
Xuanwei recounted the events in meticulous detail.
"Is it possible they were from an evil sect?" Zhang Xian asked.

"No," Li Miaoyin shook her head. "Their Dao Essence was too familiar. In Shuicheng City, the Muling Sect and the Shuiyun Sect have a long history. Neither Xuanwei nor I could mistake their techniques. They even knew the names of several senior elders. They weren't impersonators.
"The Muling Sect emphasizes harmony and tranquility. They have an excellent reputation as healers. That is exactly why we let our guard down."
Zhang Xian nodded. He remembered hearing of them during his time in Shuicheng City.
"Perhaps those disciples simply harbored malicious intent, thinking they could act without consequence in a small world," Xuanwei sighed. "If not for the tools you gave us, Duke, we would be dead."

"Two things bother me," Zhang Xian noted. "First, the Qi Refining disciple tried to kill you without mercy, but the Foundation Establishment leader held back against Miaoyin. They wanted you dead, but they wanted her alive."
"Hah, maybe they’re just as lustful as you," Yu Yun remarked dryly.

Zhang Xian ignored the jab and continued. "Second, this world has no spiritual energy. To return to the main realm, they would need to set up a costly array requiring at least thirty mid-grade spirit stones. That’s a high price for a casual visit."
Are they targeting me? he wondered. It seemed unlikely. His only real enemy was Zhao Chengyue, and if Zhao had found him, he wouldn't have sent such weak pawns.
"I need to investigate this when I return," Zhang Xian said. "If we only kill the small fry, their elders will eventually come seeking revenge. That would be a headache."
The group fell silent. Zhang Xian then pivoted the conversation. "Setting that aside... Miaoyin, have you heard of Li Fuxi?"

"That’s my family’s founding ancestor!" Li Miaoyin exclaimed. "When I was still in the Shuiyun Sect, Ancestor Fuxi was already at the mid-stage of the Golden Core. She was the top talent in Shuicheng City."
"She later joined the Yunmiao Sect and rose through the ranks. That’s why the Shuiyun Sect curried favor with us, allowing the Li family to prosper. Why do you ask?"
"I’ve joined the Yunmiao Sect myself," Zhang Xian explained. "She is currently my master. I noticed you look a bit like her."
Li Miaoyin shook her head. "I’ve seen Ancestor Fuxi once. Her beauty is peerless; I couldn't possibly compare."
"Senior Sister! What nonsense!" Xuanwei declared. "You are the most beautiful woman in my heart!"
Yu Yun rolled his eyes so hard they nearly disappeared into his skull, mentally cursing Zhang Xian again.
This guy definitely saw how beautiful their ancestor was and sprinted to become her disciple. He realized he had no hope with Senior Aunt Miaoyin and moved on to her ancestor. Outrageous!

"I have another concern," Zhang Xian said. "I've fabricated an identity as a young master from a powerful hidden world to deter enemies. But if my true name or this world’s location is exposed, the peace here will end."
"I must resolve the Muling Sect matter entirely.
"Don't be rash," Li Miaoyin cautioned. "Their Sect Master reached the mid-stage of the Golden Core over a century ago. He isn't someone you can challenge yet."
"No need to panic," Zhang replied calmly. "Three years ago, I repelled Zhao Chengyue, the head of the Zhao family. The Muling Sect is only slightly stronger than them, right?"
"The Zhao Family Head? Zhao Chengyue?" Xuanwei gasped.

"Yes. The old man tried to kill me with an array, but I forced him back. Besides, there is no 'Zhao Family' anymore. I’m good friends with the head of the Cloud Raiment Pavilion; she helped me wipe them out."
"See that flying vessel? That was a gift from her."
"The Pavilion Head... Yun Wanqing? Gave that... to you?" Xuanwei’s voice cracked.
"Indeed."
Xuanwei sucked in a sharp breath. It sounded like a fairy tale. Suddenly, he winced—Li Miaoyin had pinched him hard.
"Why are you so excited about the Pavilion Head?" she hissed. "Still thinking about other women?"
"No! Absolutely not!"
Before departing, Zhang Xian left behind a hoard of spirit stones and magical tools.
[Ding!]
A system prompt sounded. Zhang Xian pulled out a puppet and handed it to Li Miaoyin.
"Fellow Daoist Miaoyin, your cultivation is the highest here. This puppet avatar will serve as your ultimate defense."

"Equipped with spirit stones, it matches your strength. It carries high-grade tools it can detonate in an emergency. If things get dire, you can blow up the entire puppet. I’ll feel the destruction even across spatial boundaries, and I’ll come back immediately."
Li Miaoyin accepted it without ceremony. She already owed him too much for it to matter.
[Ding! Successfully gifted Mysterious-Grade Puppet Avatar. Triggering return reward: Earth-Grade Puppet Avatar x10]
[Earth-Grade Puppet Avatar: As long as the spiritual core is intact, the puppet cannot be destroyed. Capable of exerting strength surpassing the host.]
Holy crap, I struck gold! Zhang Xian was elated. Months of effort in the sect paled in comparison to a single system reward.

chapters.title: Chapter 63 I Didn’t See Anything
paragraphs: As soon as Zhang Xian returned to the flying vessel, he eagerly began studying his new puppet bodies.

The ten puppets were identical to his own disguised form. Their craftsmanship was so high that they were indistinguishable from real people. Powered by high-grade spirit stones, these puppets were formidable; by embedding five stones of the same element, a puppet's power could reach the eighth level of Foundation Establishment.
Furthermore, they possessed Supreme Spirit Roots, meaning they were entirely unrestricted by Zhang Xian's own Wood Spirit Root.

His only regret was the mental strain. At his current cultivation level, he could only operate one puppet in active combat. For simple tasks like walking or talking, he could manage two, but any more resulted in a splitting headache.
"It seems I need to enhance my spiritual sense," Zhang Xian muttered, rubbing his temples.

Zhang Xian decided to resolve the Muling Sect matter under the banner of the Yunmiao Sect. His true identity remained hidden, so he could simply claim that Xuanwei and Li Miaoyin were friends he had made while training in the minor worlds.
Piloting the vessel at full speed, he arrived back at the Yunmiao Sect in just five days.

It was already night. As he approached the spirit spring, a thin mist hung over the water. Through the haze, he vaguely made out two graceful figures with their palms pressed together. The water reached just above their delicate collarbones, sending soft ripples across the surface.
They were engaged in a form of dual cultivation, circulating spiritual energy between them to maximize their progress.

Zhang Xian, his mind still preoccupied with his puppets, looked up and saw their wet backs. Because the spring had been purified by Dragon Saliva Jade Liquid, the water was crystal clear. To make matters worse, Li Fuxi was currently facing his direction.
Zhang Xian froze on the spot.
Li Fuxi and her companion, startled by the noise, dispersed their spiritual senses. They looked up to see Zhang Xian standing on the shore, staring blankly at them.
"Ah!" Li Fuxi screamed, submerging herself instantly. A second later, she realized the water offered no concealment at all.

Before Zhang Xian could even turn his head, a sharp burst of sword energy sent him flying. The force hurled him dozens of zhang through the air until he crashed heavily into his carefully cultivated Green Spirit Vine.
With a loud Boom!, the vine reached a premature end to its life.
"What happened?"

Chen Tiexin and Zhenhai rushed over from their cottages. They found Zhang Xian groaning on the ground, with Lin Yinyin hovering over him in concern. Nearby, Li Fuxi sat by the pool, her face a mask of shame and fury.
Both Lin Yinyin and Li Fuxi were now dressed, though their hair was wet and water stains clung to their clothes. Their faces were flushed a deep crimson.
Zhenhai’s instincts screamed danger. He reacted instantly. "Huh? There’s nothing over here," he said, turning on his heel.
"Ah! Yes! Senior Brother, wait for me!" Chen Tiexin followed suit.
Two flying swords shot into the night sky, fleeing hundreds of li away from the peak.
An awkward silence hung over the stone table where the three remained.
"Brother, it's my fault. I didn't know you'd suddenly return," Lin Yinyin said, taking the blame.
Li Fuxi added resentfully, "Yinyin and I were focused on our breathing; we didn't have our spiritual senses active. But you—how did you not sense us in the spring?"
"I had other things on my mind!" Zhang Xian pleaded. "I didn't expect anyone to be in my own house! I'm innocent!"
Li Fuxi looked at him suspiciously. She was annoyed, but she knew she had no real grounds for further anger.
Lin Yinyin giggled softly. "Forget it, Master. It’s not like he saw us completely naked; we still had our undergarments on."
"You shut up!" Li Fuxi snapped.
She took a deep breath, her ears and neck still bright red. "Forget it. It’s just a physical body; I don't care."
"I... I’m going back," she said, standing up.
"Wait, Master. I have something to report."

Li Fuxi looked embarrassed, but seeing Zhang Xian’s serious expression, she reluctantly sat back down. He proceeded to recount the incident in the Great Liang Kingdom, omitting only the most sensitive details.
"I will report this to the sect so they can make a decision," she said hurriedly, before fleeing the scene once more.
The next morning, inside the hall of Wangya Zhenren.
Having received the message, Wangya summoned Elder Liu Huaigu, the head of Green Wood Peak.
"Teacher, what do you think of this?" Wangya asked.

Liu Huaigu frowned. "The Muling Sect falls under our jurisdiction. If Zhang Xian’s account is true, we must intervene. But something feels odd. I’ve met their leaders; they’ve always seemed upright. The current leader even studied under me for decades."
Wangya nodded. The Yunmiao Sect oversaw over a hundred smaller sects; it was rare for one to act so brazenly.
"Should we issue a disciple task?" Wangya suggested.
Liu Huaigu pondered for a moment. "Never mind. I’ll make the trip myself.
Wangya smiled. He knew Liu Huaigu had taken a special interest in Zhang Xian recently and was happy to do him a favor.
"According to Li Fuxi, Zhang Xian intends to go as well," Wangya added. "He is quite concerned about these friends."
"I see," Liu Huaigu nodded. "I'll handle the arrangements."
Returning to Green Wood Peak, Liu Huaigu immediately summoned his daughter, Liu Qingxuan.
"Qingxuan, I have a task for you." He repeated Zhang Xian's story.
"Ah?" Liu Qingxuan felt a wave of embarrassment. "I’ve never handled such things. Besides... if Zhang Xian is going, wouldn't it just be the two of us?"
"Aiya, your old father wants exactly that! It’s an opportunity to foster feelings. Tell me, do you dislike him?"
"Well... no, not really."
"If you don't dislike him, you like him!" Liu Huaigu slapped his thigh. "My silly girl, if you don't hurry, someone will snatch him away!"

He began counting on his fingers. "Lin Yinyin is one thing. But then the Cloud Raiment Pavilion Master delivers a flying vessel personally? They had a private meeting on that boat for hours! That Yun Wanqing girl is as clever as a ghost; she’s definitely taken a fancy to him."
"And then there’s Li Fuxi, restarting her cultivation and achieving dual Supreme Spirit Roots..."
Liu Qingxuan looked puzzled. "I heard that was due to sudden enlightenment?"

"Sudden enlightenment my foot!" Liu Huaigu cursed. "Only Spirit Sword Peak gets 'sudden enlightenment' every single day. Have you ever seen anyone else have it? And haven't you noticed? Zhang Xian hasn't come to see you lately."
Liu Qingxuan froze. It was true. The man who used to seek her guidance every few days had disappeared, leaving her feeling strangely empty.
"I... I don't know..." she whispered.
"This trip to the Muling Sect is your chance!" Liu Huaigu encouraged. "Go assist him. It’s not a major mission—just a warning and a hunt for an escaped disciple."
"Just the two of us... it's too deliberate," she said, blushing.

"Feelings require being deliberate!" Liu Huaigu paced anxiously. "Look at Lin Yinyin; she practically clings to him. You’re too slow-moving. He spent so much effort pursuing you, and you gave him nothing. No wonder he’s slacking off!"
Liu Qingxuan clenched her fists, silently steeling herself.
"Alright," she whispered. "I'll go."

"Teacher, what do you think of this?" Wangya asked.
Liu Huaigu frowned.
"The Muling Sect falls under our jurisdiction.
If Zhang Xian’s account is true, we must intervene.
But something feels odd.
I’ve met their leaders; they’ve always seemed upright.
The current leader even studied under me for decades."
Wangya nodded.
The Yunmiao Sect oversaw over a hundred smaller sects; it was rare for one to act so brazenly.
"Should we issue a disciple task?" Wangya suggested.
Liu Huaigu pondered for a moment.
"Never mind.
I’ll make the trip myself.
Wangya smiled.
He knew Liu Huaigu had taken a special interest in Zhang Xian recently and was happy to do him a favor.
"According to Li Fuxi, Zhang Xian intends to go as well," Wangya added.
"He is quite concerned about these friends."
"I see," Liu Huaigu nodded.
"I'll handle the arrangements."
Returning to Green Wood Peak, Liu Huaigu immediately summoned his daughter, Liu Qingxuan.
"Qingxuan, I have a task for you." He repeated Zhang Xian's story.
"Ah?" Liu Qingxuan felt a wave of embarrassment.
"I’ve never handled such things.
Besides... if Zhang Xian is going, wouldn't it just be the two of us?"
"Aiya, your old father wants exactly that!
It’s an opportunity to foster feelings.
Tell me, do you dislike him?"
"Well... no, not really."
"If you don't dislike him, you like him!" Liu Huaigu slapped his thigh.
"My silly girl, if you don't hurry, someone will snatch him away!"
He began counting on his fingers.
"Lin Yinyin is one thing.
But then the Cloud Raiment Pavilion Master delivers a flying vessel personally?
They had a private meeting on that boat for hours!
That Yun Wanqing girl is as clever as a ghost; she’s definitely taken a fancy to him."
"And then there’s Li Fuxi, restarting her cultivation and achieving dual Supreme Spirit Roots..."
Liu Qingxuan looked puzzled.
"I heard that was due to sudden enlightenment?"
"Sudden enlightenment my foot!" Liu Huaigu cursed.
"Only Spirit Sword Peak gets 'sudden enlightenment' every single day.
Have you ever seen anyone else have it?
And haven't you noticed?
Zhang Xian hasn't come to see you lately."
Liu Qingxuan froze.
It was true.
The man who used to seek her guidance every few days had disappeared, leaving her feeling strangely empty.
I don't know..." she whispered.
"This trip to the Muling Sect is your chance!" Liu Huaigu encouraged.
"Go assist him.
It’s not a major mission—just a warning and a hunt for an escaped disciple."
"Just the two of us... it's too deliberate," she said, blushing.
"Feelings require being deliberate!" Liu Huaigu paced anxiously.
"Look at Lin Yinyin; she practically clings to him.
You’re too slow-moving.
He spent so much effort pursuing you, and you gave him nothing.
No wonder he’s slacking off!"
Liu Qingxuan clenched her fists, silently steeling herself.
"Alright," she whispered.
"I'll go."

chapters.title: Chapter 64 I’ll Help You Keep an Eye on Him
paragraphs: The announcement that Liu Qingxuan, the supervising officer of Green Wood Peak, would embark on an external mission with Zhang Xian spread through the Yunmiao Sect like wildfire.
"What? Supervisor Liu is going out alone with Zhang Xian?"
"Does a minor dispute really require a supervising officer's personal attention? This reeks of a back-alley deal."
"How is this any different from a honeymoon? Where is Green Wood Peak’s pride?"

A disciple from Green Wood Peak added tearfully, "Our senior brother was enlightened by Sister Zhiyin and has already switched to the 'Nine Turns Jade Condensation Sutra.' His progress is astonishingly fast, but now the rest of us are like a dragon without a head!"
When the news reached Spirit Sword Peak, Lin Yinyin nearly hit the ceiling.
"Master! Have you heard? That white lotus from Green Wood Peak is going out alone with Brother. I want to go too!"

"This is a sect mission. Don't be ridiculous," Li Fuxi said calmly. "Besides, you’ve just entered the late Foundation Establishment stage. You are at the critical juncture of perfecting your core with the 'Nine Turns Jade Condensation Sutra.' You aren't going anywhere."
"Absolutely not!" Lin Yinyin shook her head violently. "I'd rather give up the sutra and my core perfection than let them go!"
She tried to bolt toward Zhang Xian’s cottage, but Li Fuxi flicked a finger. Several water-binding spells wrapped around Lin Yinyin instantly.
"Stay put and behave."

Thump. Lin Yinyin dropped to her knees and hugged Li Fuxi’s thigh, looking up with wide, watery eyes. "Master, you don't want me to become a 'gazing-at-husband' stone, do you? I won't be able to cultivate a lick like this."
"I’m so miserable... by the time they come back, Liu Qingxuan might already be pregnant with Brother’s child!"
Li Fuxi looked at her disciple’s pitiful face, feeling both annoyed and amused. "You are not leaving. Period."
"Then how about this—Master, you go keep an eye on Brother for me?"
"Me?"
"Yes! You're the only one I trust," Lin Yinyin said, spreading her hands. "Since you won't let me go, you have to watch them for me."
Li Fuxi hesitated. She knew Lin Yinyin well enough to know the girl wouldn't find a moment's peace if those two were left alone.
"Go! Your disciple’s future happiness depends on you!" Lin Yinyin began to wheedle and act coquettishly.
"Fine, fine." Li Fuxi, pestered into a headache, finally relented. She completely missed the sly, triumphant smile that flashed across Yinyin’s face.
"Master is the best!"
The next morning, as light pierced the sea of clouds, three figures boarded the vessel.
Liu Qingxuan’s skirt brushed the gangway as she gave Zhang Xian a slight, nodding smile. Li Fuxi, dressed in her silver-edged white robes, maintained a solemn, icy expression.
As the vessel soared away, wails rose from the crowd below.
"Our Supervisor Liu has fallen!"
"Supervisor Fuxi is even more beautiful than I remembered... but wait, why is she going? She’s had zero romantic rumors for a century. She’s devoted solely to the sword."
"That scoundrel Zhang Xian won't be able to make a move with his master watching him. He’ll have to restrain himself."
A young male cultivator of ordinary appearance patted the speaker on the shoulder. "Junior Brother, I’m afraid you’ve miscalculated."
"What do you mean?"

"I have exclusive inside information," the man said. This was Old Deng, the legendary intelligence chief of the Yunmiao Sect. His word was often more trusted than official sect notices. "Last night, someone spotted Supervisor Fuxi at Zhang Xian’s spirit spring. She had just finished bathing."
"!!!" The crowd’s collective expression soured as if they had swallowed flies.
"Impossible! Wouldn't Yinyin do something about that?"
Old Deng’s voice turned mournful. "The key point is... Yinyin was also there."
"Beast!" several of Li Fuxi’s long-time admirers shouted, nearly fainting.
"Taking on two at once? This is utterly depraved!"
On that day, several more disciples gave up on romance and switched to studying the "Nine Turns Jade Condensation Sutra."
Onboard the vessel, Zhang Xian gestured politely toward a cabin.
"Supervisor Liu, this room has an integrated spirit-gathering array. It should be quite comfortable.
Liu Qingxuan bowed slightly. "Thank you for your trouble." She entered her room to rest.
Zhang Xian then led Li Fuxi further into the inner cabin area. He pointed to another door. "Master, you’ll stay here. The hot spring room is right next door."
Li Fuxi’s fair face instantly flushed. "You! How could I possibly... with you—"
She bit her tongue, realizing her slip, and stopped abruptly.

"Master has misunderstood," Zhang Xian said, producing a jade vial. "I’ll be focusing on puppet research for the next few days and won't be using the spring. Please accept this Dragon Saliva Jade Liquid as a humble gift."
Li Fuxi stared at the shimmering vial. A flicker of Desire crossed her eyes before she hesitated. "No, you should keep it."
"The debt I owe for your teachings cannot be repaid," Zhang Xian said softly, placing the vial on a stone table by the door. "If you feel uneasy, consider it a simple offering from your disciple."
"I’ll head to my room now. If you need anything, just summon a maidservant."
He turned and left. Li Fuxi watched him walk away, struggling with herself, before finally taking the vial and retreating into her room with a long sigh.
[Ding! Successfully gifted Earth-grade Dragon Saliva Jade Liquid. Return triggered: 100 vials of Dragon Saliva Jade Liquid.]

Inside her quarters, Li Fuxi found the room luxuriously appointed. Sandalwood tables, a rosewood bed, and a meditation chamber with walls carved in intricate patterns. In the center lay a silk cushion, and on the back wall, a single character was inscribed: Stability.
She touched the wall; the spiritual energy here was even denser than at the peak of Spirit Sword Peak.
A maidservant puppet bowed at her door. "Honored Master, would you like to dine? The master has prepared Spirit Mist Tea and Crystal Ice Cakes. There are also fine dishes of spirit fowl."
"Just something simple," Li Fuxi replied. She rarely ate, but curiosity got the better of her.
When the puppet returned with the delicacies, Li Fuxi took a bite. Her eyes lit up. Mmm... delicious!

Once the plates were cleared, the puppet asked, "Honored Master, would you like your swords maintained? We have an artisan workshop aboard with equipment equivalent to the Cloud Raiment Pavilion’s premium services."
Li Fuxi raised an eyebrow. "You have such equipment on a ship?"
"The master says sword cultivators treat their swords as their lives," the puppet replied. "He modified a room specifically for this purpose."

chapters.title: Chapter 65 Hot Spring Reverie
paragraphs: Li Fuxi rested for a short while before she found herself unable to resist the remaining crystal ice cakes.
They were sweet and refreshing; she truly adored them.
After finishing the treats, she settled cross-legged upon a meditation cushion in the quiet room to begin her cultivation.
However, she soon discovered that tranquility eluded her.
Perhaps the environment was simply too opulent, leaving her feeling unsettled. She attempted to circulate her energy through several cycles, but her mind drifted back to the events of two days prior.
The memory of Zhang Xian stumbling upon her bathing in the hot spring flashed through her mind, followed by the vivid sensation of consuming the Immortal Ascension Pill.
"Rebellious disciple!" she muttered, her irritation growing. Even the calligraphy for "Calm" hanging on the wall seemed to mock her, only making her feel more restless.
She rose and headed for the exit. The maid stationed at the door immediately approached with a bow. "Does the True Person have any instructions?"
Li Fuxi had intended to go to the deck for some fresh air, but as she extended her spiritual sense, she detected Zhang Xian’s presence there.
Reluctant to face him, she pivoted. "Take me to the hot spring room."
The maid led her through a carved archway into a corner suite. The entire chamber was fashioned from warm jade, and the pool water glowed with a faint, milky-white luminescence.
"The spring water is replaced daily and is infused with a spiritual energy array. The True Person may activate any elemental attributes she desires," the puppet explained.
"Would the True Person care for fruits or desserts? I can fetch them for you."
Li Fuxi glanced at the puppet uneasily, feeling as though Zhang Xian’s eyes might be watching her through the construct. She waved her hand dismissively.
"You may leave. Do not enter without my permission."
"Understood. This servant shall take her leave." The puppet bowed and thoughtfully closed the door.
Li Fuxi inspected the array core of the hot spring. She found five elemental nodes: metal, wood, water, fire, and earth. To her astonishment, each node was powered by a high-grade spirit stone.
Such extravagance! She was secretly stunned; she had only used a handful of high-grade stones when she attempted to break through to the seventh level of the Golden Core.
She activated the metal and water arrays but did not enter immediately. Instead, she meticulously searched the room for any hidden mechanisms.
Still feeling cautious, she deployed several of her own concealment arrays to block any external detection.

With a hesitant hand, she produced a vial of Dragon Saliva Jade Liquid and let a single drop fall into the water. She slowly untied her sash, tested the temperature with her snow-white toes, and slid her body into the pool.
"Mmm..." She sighed as the tension bled out of her, sinking until only her eyes remained above the surface.

It felt as though a thousand warm, tiny hands were massaging her meridians. She had to admit she was becoming fond of this luxury; the comfort was immense, and the benefits to her cultivation were undeniable.
She toyed with the jade vial, sniffing the delicate fragrance of the Earth-grade treasure. Using such a rarity for a simple bath felt wasteful, yet wonderful.

Involuntarily, her mind returned to the hot spring encounter from a few days ago. Water droplets rolled down her flushed cheeks. In a daze, she imagined Zhang Xian’s smiling face reflected in the rippling water.
Absurd!
She abruptly dunked her head beneath the surface.
Out on the deck, Zhang Xian sat cross-legged. Beside him, a puppet identical to him in appearance was performing an intricate sword dance.
Under the moonlight, the puppet’s movements were fluid, its blade carving faint trails of light through the air.
"Such exquisite control!"
Liu Qingxuan appeared beside him. She pointed at the sword-wielding figure. "If he didn't possess a metal spiritual root, I wouldn't be able to tell which one was your true body."
Zhang Xian opened his eyes and stood up, though his movements were somewhat sluggish. Simultaneously, the puppet’s swordplay became stiff and mechanical.
"Neither of them is the real me," a voice called out from behind Liu Qingxuan.
The real Zhang Xian stepped out from the cabin.
Liu Qingxuan gasped, covering her mouth. "This... this is incredible! You can actually control two puppets at once?"
The moment she spoke, the puppet that had been trying to stand bumped into the one practicing swordplay. With a dull thud, both constructs collapsed into a tangled heap.
Zhang Xian offered an awkward smile. "It’s far inferior to the work of Sister Zhiyin. The captain of this ship is her creation; her puppets can manage every function of this vessel simultaneously."

Liu Qingxuan shook her head. "That is different. Zhiyin has been at the peak of the Golden Core stage for many years. To my knowledge, no Foundation Establishment student at Heavenly Puppet Peak has ever managed to control two puppets at once."
"And your puppets are so lifelike," she continued. "You’ve only been at Heavenly Puppet Peak for a few months. You have a remarkable talent for this."
"Is that so? At Green Wood Peak, I stayed for months and still couldn't recognize half the spiritual plants."
Liu Qingxuan chuckled softly. "True. You were among the most... challenged students I have ever taught."
"Perhaps you were just a poor teacher and are blaming me?" Zhang Xian teased.
"Nonsense! You simply didn't study. Who knows what you were daydreaming about every day."
As she said this, a memory seemed to strike her, and her face turned a sudden shade of crimson.
"What could I possibly have been thinking about?"
"Thinking about..." Liu Qingxuan faltered, unable to finish. She quickly changed the subject. "By the way, where is your master?"
"Making tea, perhaps. Or resting," Zhang Xian replied.
"I see."
She had intended to remark on the luxury of the ship or thank him again for his gifts, but the words failed her.
Zhang Xian stood beside her, focusing his mind to make the two puppets stand up again—one returned to a meditative pose while the other resumed its sword practice.
"Zhang Xian," Liu Qingxuan said softly, looking at his profile. "Why do you maintain this disguise? You clearly possess beauty-preserving pills."
Zhang Xian blinked in surprise before waving a hand to dispel the illusion. His original, handsome face was revealed.
"I have enemies I would rather not have recognize me," he admitted. "So? Am I handsome?"

"Just average," Liu Qingxuan teased, laughing behind her hand. "Actually, the disguise is unnecessary. Even if you hide your face, those familiar with you can recognize your spiritual fluctuations. You should use arrays to mask your presence instead."

For cultivators, beauty was common, and Zhang Xian was indeed only 'somewhat' handsome by those standards. Yet, as she looked at his easy smile, Liu Qingxuan found him increasingly pleasant to be around.
"Haha," Zhang Xian laughed. He couldn't easily explain that he was hiding from Nan Gongyao, who had known him as a mere mortal.
A gentle night breeze stirred, lifting strands of Liu Qingxuan’s hair and carrying a faint, sweet fragrance toward him.
"Zhang Xian," she asked, her voice dropping to a whisper. "Why are you so good to me?"

Zhang Xian paused, then smiled warmly. "Because you deserve it, Supervisor Liu. You are sincere and kind. You didn't look down on me because I came from an outer peak or because I practiced False Core techniques."
"Is that all?" Her voice was so quiet it nearly vanished into the wind. "Do you not want anything in return?"
He gazed out at the sea of clouds in the distance. "Supervisor Liu, when you make a friend, do you immediately calculate the profit? I follow my heart. If it feels right, I do it."
He turned back to her, a playful glint in his eyes. "Besides, you are very beautiful. It makes me happy to be friends with a beautiful lady."
"Smooth talker," she replied, laughing softly. A sense of peace settled over her, and deep within her heart, a long-silent string began to vibrate.
