chapters.title: Chapter 91 You Sure Know How to Comfort Someone
paragraphs: The fourth bolt of heavenly lightning had barely faded when the tribulation clouds surged downward, nearly grinding against the peak of Qiongxiao. Within the churning violet mists, thousands of electric serpents writhed in a frantic dance, filling the air with a bone-chilling crackle.
Lin Yinyin fumbled with her storage pouch, pulling out a handful of pills. Without bothering to count them, she shoved the entire lot into her mouth.
The medicinal essence dissolved instantly, sending a warm current through her limbs, but her hands wouldn't stop shaking. She could barely keep her grip on the jade bottle.

At the Golden Core stage, heavenly lightning possessed a terrifying suppressive property against defensive treasures and talismans. To survive, a cultivator had to rely on the raw strength of their own foundation.
The onlookers held their breath, their eyes locked on the sky. This tribulation was far more violent than anything they had faced in their own youth.
A realization dawned on the crowd: Lin Yinyin’s talent wasn't just a Supreme Spirit Root. It was something far more monstrous.
Boom!
A muffled roar from the clouds rattled her internal organs until they bled. Suddenly, the sky split open like a jagged wound.
The fifth bolt descended—a pillar of eerie, violet-black lightning thicker than the previous four combined.
Pfft!
Lin Yinyin sprayed a mouthful of blood, her face turning deathly pale in an instant.
"Yinyin!" Zhang Xian and Li Fuxi cried out in unison.
Before she could even gasp for air, the sixth bolt coiled in the heavens, ready to strike. At the brink of death, a blinding radiance erupted from Lin Yinyin’s body.
The Nine Turns Jade Condensation Sutra roared to life, operating at its absolute maximum capacity.

A jade-like chime echoed through the heavens. A brilliant, glazed radiance wrapped around her, barely buffering the impact of the lightning. In her dantian, a profound aura condensed into a million points of light.
"This is..." Wang Ya’s pupils contracted sharply.
Within Lin Yinyin’s dantian, a Golden Core as clear as glazed jade was taking shape. Five-colored light swirled within its core, while its surface was etched with ancient, mysterious patterns.
"A Fifth-Grade Golden Core!" Shouheng Zhenren shouted, unable to contain his shock.
The clouds began to thin, but the phenomenon didn't stop. To the east, a trail of violet qi stretched majestically for three thousand miles.
Li Fuxi watched with tears in her eyes. It was truly a Fifth-Grade Golden Core. She felt more joy now than she had during her own breakthrough.
Zhang Xian let out a long breath, though he was secretly green with envy.
Seeing the sheer power of that lightning had left his back soaked in cold sweat. He was terrified; if he had been the one under those clouds, he would have been reduced to ash.
Elder Zhiyin seemed to read his thoughts. "Don't worry," she offered, trying to be helpful. "With your False Core, the tribulation will only be three strikes at most."
Zhang Xian: "..."
"You sure know how to comfort someone," he muttered.
Lin Yinyin opened her eyes, a weak smile playing on her lips. "Brother... I did it..."
The world spun, and she pitched forward. Su Ling blurred across the ground, catching her before she hit the dirt.
"So this is the Heavenly Tribulation of the humans," Su Ling whispered. "Facing death to find new life."
Zhang Xian flew over and scooped Yinyin into his arms. She was covered in cuts and burns, but her breathing was steady. She had simply pushed herself to the point of collapse.
He gently wiped the blood from her cheek. "Silly girl," he whispered. "You’re really amazing."
When Lin Yinyin finally woke up, she was back in the familiar bedroom of the flying vessel.
"You're awake?"
Li Fuxi sat by the bed, smiling gently.
"Master..." Lin Yinyin tried to sit up, but her muscles felt like lead.
"Don't rush. Your Golden Core just formed. You need time to stabilize your realm."
Lin Yinyin’s eyes widened with sudden panic. "Where's my brother?"
"After your tribulation ended, he felt his own breakthrough coming. He left yesterday to prepare for his own crossing."
"What?!" Lin Yinyin bolted upright, ignoring the weakness. "He went alone? Is there anyone guarding him? What if something goes wrong?"
Li Fuxi patted her hand. "Relax. His tribulation won't be like yours. I doubt the lightning could even make a scratch on his defensive treasures."
Lin Yinyin looked down at her own palm. She could feel the vast, crystalline power of the Fifth-Grade Golden Core rotating in her inner palace.
In a few short years, she had gone from a common Qi Refining girl to a world-class genius. She should have been celebrating, but thinking of her brother made her heart sink.
"Master... Brother's False Core... at best, it’s only as strong as a First-Grade Golden Core, right?"
Li Fuxi went quiet for a moment before nodding. "The False Core technique ultimately has its limits."
She quickly changed the subject. "Yinyin, do you realize your Fifth-Grade Golden Core is the talk of the Southern Region? Right now, you're more famous than the Demon Sweeping Assembly itself.
Lin Yinyin touched her dantian, feeling the gentle glow of the jade core.
"Master..." she hesitated. "About the Nine Turns Jade Condensation Sutra..."
Li Fuxi’s expression turned stern. "Yinyin, have you thought this through? With your talent, reaching the Nascent Soul stage is a certainty if you continue this path."
Her voice dropped to a whisper. "In all of the Southern Region, there are fewer than ten Nascent Soul cultivators."
Lin Yinyin looked out the window at the sea of clouds, her gaze hardening.
"Master, have you ever truly liked someone?"
Li Fuxi froze, caught off guard by the question.

"If I cannot be with my brother," Lin Yinyin continued softly but firmly, "then I don't care about the Nascent Soul stage. Everything I have, he gave to me. I only cultivated this sutra for him. I can't wait decades for 'great success' while he moves on without me."
She was tired of being the protected little sister. She wanted to stand by his side like Liu Qingxuan—or like her Master.
Li Fuxi sighed, knowing she couldn't change the girl's mind. The room fell into a long silence.
Finally, Li Fuxi’s face flushed a strange shade of pink.

"Then... then you still can't be with Zhang Xian that quickly," she murmured, her voice getting smaller. "At the very least, you must reach the second layer of the Golden Core stage. If the sutra is broken before then, your cultivation will plummet a whole major realm."
Lin Yinyin’s face turned crimson all the way to her ears. She buried her head in her chest. "I... I understand."
A month later, Zhang Xian returned, looking weary and covered in the dust of the road.
Li Fuxi and Lin Yinyin were practicing in the vessel's sword chamber when they heard his footsteps.
He stood in the doorway, his silhouette tall and straight. The spiritual energy radiating from him was significantly stronger than before, but...
Even Lin Yinyin could feel the difference. The energy was abundant, but it lacked the perfect, seamless flow of a true core.
A False Core was still just a False Core—the equivalent of a bottom-tier First-Grade. Her heart ached, and her eyes grew hot involuntarily.
Zhang Xian saw their long faces and shrugged with a grin. "What’s with those looks? A False Core is still a Golden Core."
He struck a theatrical pose. "Just like you geniuses, I’ve got at least a thousand years of life to burn now. What’s the rush?"
Li Fuxi thought of his history—how he had been trapped at the Innate Realm for nearly a century.
A sense of peace washed over her. He was right; they had time.
Zhang Xian was a man who specialized in miracles. Just because no one in the Southern Region had ever pushed past a False Core didn't mean he wouldn't be the first.

I doubt the lightning could even make a scratch on his defensive treasures."
Lin Yinyin looked down at her own palm.
She could feel the vast, crystalline power of the Fifth-Grade Golden Core rotating in her inner palace.
In a few short years, she had gone from a common Qi Refining girl to a world-class genius.
She should have been celebrating, but thinking of her brother made her heart sink.
"Master...
Brother's False Core... at best, it’s only as strong as a First-Grade Golden Core, right?"
Li Fuxi went quiet for a moment before nodding.
"The False Core technique ultimately has its limits."
She quickly changed the subject.
"Yinyin, do you realize your Fifth-Grade Golden Core is the talk of the Southern Region?
Right now, you're more famous than the Demon Sweeping Assembly itself.
Lin Yinyin touched her dantian, feeling the gentle glow of the jade core.
"Master..." she hesitated.
"About the Nine Turns Jade Condensation Sutra..."
Li Fuxi’s expression turned stern.
"Yinyin, have you thought this through?
With your talent, reaching the Nascent Soul stage is a certainty if you continue this path."
Her voice dropped to a whisper.
"In all of the Southern Region, there are fewer than ten Nascent Soul cultivators."
Lin Yinyin looked out the window at the sea of clouds, her gaze hardening.
"Master, have you ever truly liked someone?"
Li Fuxi froze, caught off guard by the question.
"If I cannot be with my brother," Lin Yinyin continued softly but firmly, "then I don't care about the Nascent Soul stage.
Everything I have, he gave to me.
I only cultivated this sutra for him.
I can't wait decades for 'great success' while he moves on without me."
She was tired of being the protected little sister.
She wanted to stand by his side like Liu Qingxuan—or like her Master.
Li Fuxi sighed, knowing she couldn't change the girl's mind.
The room fell into a long silence.
Finally, Li Fuxi’s face flushed a strange shade of pink.
"Then... then you still can't be with Zhang Xian that quickly," she murmured, her voice getting smaller.
"At the very least, you must reach the second layer of the Golden Core stage.
If the sutra is broken before then, your cultivation will plummet a whole major realm."
Lin Yinyin’s face turned crimson all the way to her ears.
She buried her head in her chest.
I understand."
A month later, Zhang Xian returned, looking weary and covered in the dust of the road.
Li Fuxi and Lin Yinyin were practicing in the vessel's sword chamber when they heard his footsteps.
He stood in the doorway, his silhouette tall and straight.
The spiritual energy radiating from him was significantly stronger than before, but...
Even Lin Yinyin could feel the difference.
The energy was abundant, but it lacked the perfect, seamless flow of a true core.
A False Core was still just a False Core—the equivalent of a bottom-tier First-Grade.
Her heart ached, and her eyes grew hot involuntarily.
Zhang Xian saw their long faces and shrugged with a grin.
"What’s with those looks?
A False Core is still a Golden Core."
He struck a theatrical pose.
"Just like you geniuses, I’ve got at least a thousand years of life to burn now.
What’s the rush?"
Li Fuxi thought of his history—how he had been trapped at the Innate Realm for nearly a century.
A sense of peace washed over her.
He was right; they had time.
Zhang Xian was a man who specialized in miracles.
Just because no one in the Southern Region had ever pushed past a False Core didn't mean he wouldn't be the first.

chapters.title: Chapter 92 Some Things Cannot Be Replaced by Puppets
paragraphs: "Brother!"
Lin Yinyin lunged forward, throwing herself into Zhang Xian's arms and rubbing her cheek against his chest with clingy abandon. "I missed you so much."
She looked up at him, her eyes shimmering with a bold, predatory heat. "Once I stabilize my realm, we can finally—"
Zhang Xian chuckled, ruffling her hair to stifle her words. "What about the Nine Turns Jade Condensation Sutra? I heard that breaking your cultivation prematurely is agonizing. Aren't you afraid?"
"With you? Not even a little!"
"Ahem!"
Li Fuxi let out a series of sharp, exaggerated coughs. "Yinyin! Have you already forgotten my warning? No mischief until your foundation is perfectly set!"

Lin Yinyin stuck out her tongue and playfully bounded away from Zhang Xian. She unsheathed her longsword, the blade humming with a sharp, resonant power. "Come on, Brother Zhang Xian. Why don't we spar?"
Zhang Xian raised an eyebrow, drawing a high-grade spirit sword of his own. "Fine. Let me see what a legendary fifth-grade Golden Core is actually capable of."
"Oh?" Lin Yinyin looked him up and down, a mischievous glint in her eyes. "Are you going to fight me personally, Brother? No puppets this time?"
Zhang Xian twirled his sword, a dominant, suggestive smirk playing on his lips. "Some things," he said, his gaze lingering on her with deliberate intent, "simply cannot be replaced by puppets."
He leveled the tip of his blade at her. "For the important tasks, I always handle things personally."
Lin Yinyin froze as the double meaning hit her like a physical blow. Her face turned a vivid, stunning crimson. "Pah! You... you big pervert! Take this!"
The spirit blades clashed, ringing out in a series of crisp, rhythmic strikes.
Li Fuxi stood on the sidelines, watching her two disciples trade blows. She shook her head at their shameless flirting, but a faint, affectionate smile remained hidden deep within her eyes.
The Yunmiao Sect’s Seventy-Two Peak Competition arrived exactly as scheduled.

The event was held at the sect’s main summit, Heavenly Palace Peak. Li Fuxi, whose "Master" dignity was already crumbling under Zhang Xian’s constant advances, was the first to flee the flying vessel. She retreated to the seclusion of Spirit Sword Peak to hide her blushing face.
To keep Lin Yinyin out of trouble, she dragged the girl along with her. Left with no other choice, Zhang Xian followed them back to the familiar, humble thatched cottage on their mountaintop.
On the first day of the tournament, Zhang Xian arrived at Heavenly Palace Peak by sword-flight. The massive square was already a roiling sea of disciples.
The competition was divided into eight brackets: Groups A through Xin. Only the top fighter from each group would advance to the finals.

The format was single-elimination—a brutal ladder where the top three finishers would receive massive rewards and the honor of representing the Yunmiao Sect at the Southern Region's Demon Sweeping Assembly.
Zhang Xian had played it smart, purchasing a detailed intelligence report on every participant from Old Deng. He was placed in Group A, designated as participant A32.

The representatives from Spirit Sword Peak were strategically scattered. Chen Tiexin and Zhen Hai were in their own brackets, while Li Fuxi was in Group Wu and Lin Yinyin in Group Ji. Zhang Xian scanned the list and felt a cold smirk touch his lips—Nangong Yao was in Group Geng.
Since Zhang Xian was the final seed in his group, he had to wait through seven matches before his turn.
As he watched the fights unfold, he found himself unimpressed.

Though these disciples had higher cultivation realms than his own, the Southern Region had been peaceful for too long. Their techniques were flashy and ornamental—more like a choreographed dance than a life-or-death struggle.
Compared to the bloody, desperate battles Zhang Xian had survived in the mortal world, these matches lacked lethality. They were playing at war; he had lived it.
"Eighth Match, Group A: Number 31 versus Number 32!"

Zhang Xian walked onto the platform with measured, steady steps. His opponent was a disciple from Cloud Breaking Peak named Zhao Ming. The young man looked terrified, his sword hand trembling visibly.
"Zhang Xian, Spirit Sword Peak. I seek your guidance."
"Z-Zhao Ming... Cloud Breaking Peak... I seek yours."
According to Old Deng’s notes, Zhao Ming was a first-level Golden Core who had broken through six months ago. On paper, they were evenly matched.
However, Zhao Ming wasn't nervous because of the cultivation gap. He was nervous because Zhang the Old Fiend’s reputation preceded him.
Rumor had it he had already "ravaged" the sect’s most beautiful women. Worse, losing to a "watered-down" False Core cultivator would be a mark of shame that would haunt Zhao Ming forever.
"Begin!" the referee shouted.

Zhang Xian’s sword hissed out of its sheath. He didn't use any expensive talismans or flashy tricks. Instead, he executed the fundamental forms of the Yunmiao Sword Scripture with terrifying, clinical precision.
The sword became an extension of his will, each thrust finding the gaps in Zhao Ming’s shaky defense.
Despite being a dedicated sword cultivator, Zhao Ming was utterly suppressed from the very first breath.
"Wait, look!" someone whispered from the crowd. "That old lecher's swordsmanship is actually... incredible."
"Hmph, I bet Inspector Fuxi gives him 'private lessons' every single night," another disciple grumbled, his voice thick with jealousy. "I wish I were the one getting suppressed by her!"
In under twenty moves, Zhang Xian flicked his wrist. Zhao Ming’s sword spun through the air, clattering onto the stone tiles. Zhang Xian’s blade came to rest precisely against the boy's chest.
"You lose," Zhang Xian said calmly.
Zhao Ming turned deathly pale. He hadn't just lost; he had been dismantled in the one discipline he prided himself on.
"Group A, Number 32 is the winner!"
Boos immediately erupted from the stands.
"Pathetic! How do you lose to a False Core?"
"Whatever, let the villain have his fun. He won't survive the next round!
Zhang Xian ignored the noise. As he stepped off the stage, he felt a message talisman vibrate. It was from Chen Tiexin.
Junior Brother, meet us at the back mountain platform. We need to talk.
When he arrived, Chen Tiexin and Zhen Hai were already waiting.
"Congrats on the win, Junior Brother!" Chen Tiexin chirped. "You’ve only been on the mountain a short while and you’re already a Golden Core. Your progress is terrifying."
"It's just a False Core," Zhang Xian replied dismissively. "How did your matches go?"
"We won, obviously," Zhen Hai said, puffing out his chest. "But Yinyin’s match is delayed. The earlier fights are moving like snails."
"Master won with a single strike and went straight back to Spirit Sword Peak," Chen Tiexin added.
That sounded exactly like Li Fuxi.
Chen Tiexin leaned in, her voice turning mysterious. "Junior Brother, do you know you're the most popular topic in the sect right now?"
"Popular?"
"Oh, absolutely. Sign-ups for this competition doubled the moment people heard you were entering. Everyone wants a piece of you."
Zhang Xian sighed. "I assume this is because of Yinyin and Liu Qingxuan?"

"Not just them," Chen Tiexin said with a smirk. "It's Master. The rumor mill says you 'drained' her through dual cultivation, which is why her realm fell. They say you keep her captive on your flying vessel for nightly revelry."
"Pfft!" Zhang Xian nearly choked. "That’s slander! Wait... how do they even know she was on the flying boat?"
"I told them," Chen Tiexin said matter-of-factly. "I’m a senior member of the Demon Exorcism Association now. I have to provide intel."
"The... the what?"

"The 'Alliance Association for Expelling Zhang the Old Lecher,'" Chen Tiexin explained proudly. "We just call it the Demon Exorcism Association for short. We spend our meetings researching how to deal with you."
Zhang Xian stared at her, speechless.
"Don't worry," she whispered, patting his arm. "I’ll feed you any updates I get. I have to go now; the secret meeting starts in ten minutes."
As she hurried away, Zhang Xian turned to Zhen Hai. "Senior Brother, please tell me you aren't part of this."

"We shouldn't be seen together in public," Zhen Hai said, patting Zhang Xian’s shoulder with a look of mock pity. "I forgot to mention—I’m actually the honorary vice president. Tonight, I’m giving a lecture on the flaws in your footwork."
Zhang Xian: "..."

chapters.title: Chapter 93 I Won’t Lose in a Battle of Endurance
paragraphs: The next day, Zhang Xian was matched against Contestant Jia-29, an Earth Spiritual Root cultivator named Wang. Known for his stubbornness, Wang didn't waste a heartbeat. The moment the match began, he summoned a massive earthen shield, creating a flawless, impenetrable fortress of stone.
"Junior Brother Wang’s defense is absolute!" someone roared from the crowd. "Let’s see how that old scoundrel Zhang Xian tries to break through this!"

Wang watched Zhang Xian with narrowed, cautious eyes. The night before, the Demon Exorcism Association had held an emergency strategy session that lasted until dawn. Their conclusion was simple: they would beat Zhang Xian at his own game. They were going to force him into a grueling battle of endurance.

As a second-level Golden Core expert, Wang was a human mountain. He was a self-made man who had clawed his way into the inner sect through sheer grit. His obsession had begun the moment he saw a recording of Li Fuxi; since then, he had spent his meager savings on every illustrated album and piece of merchandise featuring her.

When he heard that Li Fuxi was being "kept" by Zhang Xian on a flying vessel, Wang nearly suffered a mental collapse. Devastated, he found solace in the Demon Exorcism Association. He hadn't even planned on entering the tournament until he saw Zhang Xian’s name on the roster. He had signed up out of pure, unadulterated spite.

Fortune favored the vengeful. He had drawn the "Old Scoundrel" in the very second round. Even as the higher-level cultivator, Wang felt no shame in hiding behind a shield. A true man knew when to turtle up.

Wang was brimming with confidence. He had the backing of the Association, the support of the crowd, and secret intel provided by Zhen Hai and Chen Tiexin. Even the sect's intelligence chief, Old Deng, was helping them. With the world on his side, losing felt mathematically impossible.

Zhang Xian, unbothered by the spectacle, traced a lazy flourish with his sword and closed the distance. Wang smirked behind his shield. This played right into his hands. He knew Zhang Xian practiced the Azure Emperor's Rejuvenation Art, but in a war of attrition, his own Wutu Longevity Sutra was the undisputed king.
Half an hour passed. The spiritual energy in Zhang Xian’s body began to visibly flag.
"Ha! The old scoundrel is running dry!"
"Is that it? He’s not very 'enduring,' is he?"
The disciples below grew giddy with anticipation. Zhang Xian merely retracted his sword and calmly pulled out a top-grade Spirit Recovery Pill, popping it like candy.
"Holy crap! He’s taking pills!"
"Shameless! Disqualify the cheater!"

The referee ignored the shouting. In professional tournaments, pills and talismans were fair game—otherwise, alchemists and talisman masters would never win a fight. A cultivator's wealth was simply another form of power.

While the disciples grumbled, the referee’s eyes twitched. That wasn't just any pill; it was a top-grade Spirit Recovery Pill worth nearly a thousand mid-grade spirit stones. Using such a life-saving treasure for a tournament match was the definition of "burning money."

Zhang Xian ignored the noise and went back to work. Another thirty minutes passed. Wang was now drenched in sweat, his legs starting to buckle under the constant pressure. Zhang Xian, meanwhile, looked refreshed. He was actually enjoying the target practice. He swallowed a second pill.
The crowd went dead silent for a heartbeat.
"He’s cheating again!
"Impossible! No pill is that potent. I demand an investigation!"
The referee, seeing the mob starting to turn, finally spoke up: "The pill is a genuine top-grade Spirit Recovery Pill. It is within the rules."
"Curse these rich people!"
"Junior Brother Wang, hold on! Be a man!"
Another half-hour passed. Zhang Xian took his third pill. Wang’s faith finally shattered. His vision went dark, and he collapsed in a heap, unconscious from sheer mental and physical exhaustion.
"Contestant Jia-32 wins!"
Zhang Xian clasped his fists with a mock-polite smile. "Apologies for the disappointment, senior brothers. But when it comes to endurance, I never lose."
A chorus of curses followed him off the stage. Just as the vitriol reached a fever pitch, a commotion broke out. Lin Yinyin had finished her own match and arrived to greet him.
"Brother, you were amazing!" Without a hint of shame, Lin Yinyin threw herself into his arms, snuggling against him. They shared a sickeningly sweet moment before walking away together.
"Filthy beast!"
"Junior Sister Yinyin, look at me! I’m more handsome! I’m more loyal! Why him?!"
The disciples were forced to swallow a massive serving of public affection, stamping their feet in despair.

Over the next few days, Zhang Xian cruised through the brackets. In one match, he used two consecutive Profound-grade talismans—effectively throwing a small fortune at his opponent—to blast them off the stage. In the next, he lured his opponent into a melee before summoning a puppet to deliver a blindside hit.

Meanwhile, Li Fuxi maintained her "one sword" streak. Even a fifth-level Golden Core Inspector couldn't survive more than a single strike from her. Lin Yinyin was equally dominant, crushing a third-level sword cultivator and leaving the man questioning his entire life.
Unfortunately, both Zhen Hai and Chen Tiexin were knocked out in the later rounds.

Finally, the day of the group finals arrived. Zhang Xian stood on the platform, facing Lu Rending of Green Wood Peak. Lu wore dark green robes, a jade flute at his waist, and an expression of pure, righteous fury.

Green Wood Peak hated Zhang Xian more than anyone. Their beloved Inspector Liu had been "defiled" by his despicable tricks, her Nine Turns Jade Condensation Sutra shattered. She was still in seclusion, trying to piece her cultivation back together.
Lu Rending stepped forward and bowed stiffly. "Junior Brother Zhang."
Zhang Xian returned the gesture with casual grace.
"Actually, I should thank you," Lu Rending said with a cold, calm smile. "If not for you, I might never have broken my emotional shackles and switched to the Nine Turns Jade Condensation Sutra."
"To seek the Great Dao, one must sever all ties," Lu continued, his voice rising with dramatic flair. "Women only slow the speed of my blade!"
"Then congratulations are in order, Senior Brother Lu."
"However! For the honor of Green Wood Peak, and to avenge my brothers, this ends today!" Lu Rending’s aura exploded as he pointed his finger at Zhang Xian.

He was brimming with confidence. He had achieved minor mastery in the Nine Turns Jade Condensation Sutra and reached the fourth level of the Golden Core stage. He felt like the protagonist of a heroic epic—specifically, the kind of "hero overcomes the villain" story his brother, Lu Renbing, liked to write.
"Group A Finals: Contestant Jia-7 versus Contestant Jia-32!"
The crowd roared. Lu Rending attacked instantly. With a wave of his sleeve, two emerald, tree-like phantoms materialized, their branches lashing out like venomous snakes.
Simultaneously, he brought the jade flute to his lips. The melody transformed into invisible sonic blades, forming a lethal net of sound and wood.
"The Green Tide Life and Death Art!" someone screamed in delight.

Zhang Xian hurriedly slapped down several Earth Spirit Talismans. Thick walls erupted from the stage, but the sonic blades sliced through them like paper. He had to burn Wind Talismans next, his body swaying like a willow leaf as he dodged the relentless onslaught.
"Look at him! He can only run!"
"External items can't bridge a three-level gap in cultivation!"
Zhang Xian summoned a puppet, its giant sword barely holding the phantom trees at bay. Seeing a gap, he popped another top-grade Spirit Recovery Pill.

Lu Rending sneered. A brilliant green light erupted from his body, pulsing with raw vitality. "You want to play the endurance game? I'll bury you! I also know the Azure Emperor's Rejuvenation Art, and my mastery dwarfs yours!"
Lu’s spiritual energy seemed bottomless, triggering another wave of cheers.
"Senior Brother Lu is invincible!"
"His Rejuvenation Art is so powerful he's recovering faster than he's spending! He's a perpetual motion machine!"

"Is that it?
He’s not very 'enduring,' is he?"
The disciples below grew giddy with anticipation.
Zhang Xian merely retracted his sword and calmly pulled out a top-grade Spirit Recovery Pill, popping it like candy.
"Holy crap!
He’s taking pills!"
"Shameless!
Disqualify the cheater!"
The referee ignored the shouting.
In professional tournaments, pills and talismans were fair game—otherwise, alchemists and talisman masters would never win a fight.
A cultivator's wealth was simply another form of power.
While the disciples grumbled, the referee’s eyes twitched.
That wasn't just any pill; it was a top-grade Spirit Recovery Pill worth nearly a thousand mid-grade spirit stones.
Using such a life-saving treasure for a tournament match was the definition of "burning money."
Zhang Xian ignored the noise and went back to work.
Another thirty minutes passed.
Wang was now drenched in sweat, his legs starting to buckle under the constant pressure.
Zhang Xian, meanwhile, looked refreshed.
He was actually enjoying the target practice.
He swallowed a second pill.
The crowd went dead silent for a heartbeat.
"He’s cheating again!
"Impossible!
No pill is that potent.
I demand an investigation!"
The referee, seeing the mob starting to turn, finally spoke up: "The pill is a genuine top-grade Spirit Recovery Pill.
It is within the rules."
"Curse these rich people!"
"Junior Brother Wang, hold on!
Be a man!"
Another half-hour passed.
Zhang Xian took his third pill.
Wang’s faith finally shattered.
His vision went dark, and he collapsed in a heap, unconscious from sheer mental and physical exhaustion.
"Contestant Jia-32 wins!"
Zhang Xian clasped his fists with a mock-polite smile.
"Apologies for the disappointment, senior brothers.
But when it comes to endurance, I never lose."
A chorus of curses followed him off the stage.
Just as the vitriol reached a fever pitch, a commotion broke out.
Lin Yinyin had finished her own match and arrived to greet him.
"Brother, you were amazing!" Without a hint of shame, Lin Yinyin threw herself into his arms, snuggling against him.
They shared a sickeningly sweet moment before walking away together.
"Filthy beast!"
"Junior Sister Yinyin, look at me!
I’m more handsome!
I’m more loyal!
Why him?!"
The disciples were forced to swallow a massive serving of public affection, stamping their feet in despair.
Over the next few days, Zhang Xian cruised through the brackets.
In one match, he used two consecutive Profound-grade talismans—effectively throwing a small fortune at his opponent—to blast them off the stage.
In the next, he lured his opponent into a melee before summoning a puppet to deliver a blindside hit.
Meanwhile, Li Fuxi maintained her "one sword" streak.
Even a fifth-level Golden Core Inspector couldn't survive more than a single strike from her.
Lin Yinyin was equally dominant, crushing a third-level sword cultivator and leaving the man questioning his entire life.
Unfortunately, both Zhen Hai and Chen Tiexin were knocked out in the later rounds.
Finally, the day of the group finals arrived.
Zhang Xian stood on the platform, facing Lu Rending of Green Wood Peak.
Lu wore dark green robes, a jade flute at his waist, and an expression of pure, righteous fury.
Green Wood Peak hated Zhang Xian more than anyone.
Their beloved Inspector Liu had been "defiled" by his despicable tricks, her Nine Turns Jade Condensation Sutra shattered.
She was still in seclusion, trying to piece her cultivation back together.
Lu Rending stepped forward and bowed stiffly.
"Junior Brother Zhang."
Zhang Xian returned the gesture with casual grace.
"Actually, I should thank you," Lu Rending said with a cold, calm smile.
"If not for you, I might never have broken my emotional shackles and switched to the Nine Turns Jade Condensation Sutra."
"To seek the Great Dao, one must sever all ties," Lu continued, his voice rising with dramatic flair.
"Women only slow the speed of my blade!"
"Then congratulations are in order, Senior Brother Lu."
"However!
For the honor of Green Wood Peak, and to avenge my brothers, this ends today!" Lu Rending’s aura exploded as he pointed his finger at Zhang Xian.
He was brimming with confidence.
He had achieved minor mastery in the Nine Turns Jade Condensation Sutra and reached the fourth level of the Golden Core stage.
He felt like the protagonist of a heroic epic—specifically, the kind of "hero overcomes the villain" story his brother, Lu Renbing, liked to write.
"Group A Finals: Contestant Jia-7 versus Contestant Jia-32!"
The crowd roared.
Lu Rending attacked instantly.
With a wave of his sleeve, two emerald, tree-like phantoms materialized, their branches lashing out like venomous snakes.
Simultaneously, he brought the jade flute to his lips.
The melody transformed into invisible sonic blades, forming a lethal net of sound and wood.
"The Green Tide Life and Death Art!" someone screamed in delight.
Zhang Xian hurriedly slapped down several Earth Spirit Talismans.
Thick walls erupted from the stage, but the sonic blades sliced through them like paper.
He had to burn Wind Talismans next, his body swaying like a willow leaf as he dodged the relentless onslaught.
"Look at him!
He can only run!"
"External items can't bridge a three-level gap in cultivation!"
Zhang Xian summoned a puppet, its giant sword barely holding the phantom trees at bay.
Seeing a gap, he popped another top-grade Spirit Recovery Pill.
Lu Rending sneered.
A brilliant green light erupted from his body, pulsing with raw vitality.
"You want to play the endurance game?
I'll bury you!
I also know the Azure Emperor's Rejuvenation Art, and my mastery dwarfs yours!"
Lu’s spiritual energy seemed bottomless, triggering another wave of cheers.
"Senior Brother Lu is invincible!"
"His Rejuvenation Art is so powerful he's recovering faster than he's spending!
He's a perpetual motion machine!"

chapters.title: Chapter 94 It’s Been So Long Since We Soaked Alone
paragraphs: Zhang Xian managed to endure for another several minutes, playing the part of a cornered animal to perfection.
He burned a Wind Talisman to retreat to the very edge of the arena, letting out a heavy, staged sigh. "Forget it."
To the spectators, that sigh was the white flag of surrender. The crowd beneath the stage erupted instantly in a cacophony of jeers.
"Senior Brother Lu, finish him!"
"Don't give the scoundrel a chance to concede!"
"Whip him! Get revenge for every man in the Demon Exorcism Association!"
"Junior Brother, just go lie down for half a month!"
A predatory smile curled Lu Rending's lips. The tree-branch shadows surged wildly, lashing toward Zhang Xian like a venomous dragon erupting from its cave.
Thud!

A dull, heavy sound echoed, and a thousand pairs of eyes widened in disbelief. Those branches—powerful enough to shred a mid-stage Golden Core cultivator—were stopped dead three feet in front of Zhang Xian by a shimmering barrier of spiritual light.
"Impossible!" Lu Rending’s smile froze.
The stands fell into a deathly silence. Everyone held their breath as the air grew heavy with a sudden, sharp pressure.
Then, an even more shocking sight unfolded. An emerald-green longsword appeared in Zhang Xian’s hand, its blade pulsing with a heart-stopping, frigid gleam.
With a casual flick of his wrist, the sword light shot forth like a white rainbow piercing the sun.
Pfft!

Lu Rending's protective spiritual light shattered like wet paper. His entire body was launched backward by the sheer momentum of the strike, crashing heavily outside the arena like a kite with a snapped string.
A suffocating stillness enveloped the platform.
"D-did I see that right?"
"Senior Brother Lu... was one-shotted?"
"How is this possible!? I’m reporting this! That thief Zhang is cheating! He must be using some demonic technique!" an outraged disciple screamed.
The referee's voice trembled slightly. "Number thirty-two... wins."
As a peak Golden Core elder, his eyes were fixed solely on the weapon in Zhang Xian's hand. While the average disciple couldn't tell, he knew immediately: that was a Spirit Treasure.
Only a Spirit Treasure possessed that kind of speed and the raw power to utterly ignore the defense of a top-grade magical instrument.
Moreover, Zhang Xian likely had more than one. The barrier that had blocked Lu Rending’s Green Tide Life and Death Art was almost certainly a defensive Spirit Treasure as well.
The referee himself didn't own a Spirit Treasure; even Vice Sect Leader Wang Ya didn't have one. This False Core disciple was walking around with at least two? The world had gone mad.

Zhang Xian walked slowly to the edge of the stage, looking down at the unconscious Lu Rending. He murmured softly, "Sorry, Senior Brother Lu. It looks like you'll be the one lying down for half a month."
The stands exploded into a chaotic uproar of confusion and fury.
"How arrogant!"
"Senior Brother Lu was just careless!"
"Nonsense! Which of you could have survived that sword strike?"
"In three days, the champion of Group A will face the champion of Group B," the referee elder announced, his voice struggling to be heard over the noise.
Spirit Sword Peak, Evening.
Zhang Xian sat on a stone stool in the courtyard, sighing softly. "It’s still too early."
He had intended to hide his true strength until the final showdown—a little "surprise" for Nangong Yao.
Unfortunately, Lu Rending was the real deal, not a fraud like Zhao Chengyue. The Green Tide Life and Death Art was formidable enough that Zhang Xian couldn't win without dipping into his trump cards.
Now the entire Yunmiao Sect knew he possessed a heavy treasure. His future opponents would be on high guard, making it much harder to catch them off-balance.
"Brother!"
Lin Yinyin’s voice drifted in from the gate, vibrating with unbridled excitement. Zhang Xian stood up just as she rushed into his arms, tilting her small face up to his.
"Congratulations, Brother, on taking first place in Group A!"
"Master swept Group Wu, and I managed to snag first in Group Ji!" she chirped. "Spirit Sword Peak took three of the eight brackets. Master is glowing."
"That’s good. We’ll fight all the way to the top and represent the sect together."
Lin Yinyin stuck out her tongue, her expression suddenly sagging. "But I’ve hit my limit! In three days, I have to face Master. It’s a death sentence!"
Zhang Xian ruffled her soft hair, his eyes full of affection. "How old are you? The next tournament will be your stage. By then, you'll be cutting through the competition with ease."
"Hmph!"
Lin Yinyin wrinkled her nose, stood on her tiptoes, and planted a loud, wet kiss on his cheek. "It’s all because you supported me, Brother. Otherwise, I’d still be stuck in the mines."
Zhang Xian laughed and pulled her closer. Her warm, soft lips eventually met his, carrying a familiar, sweet fragrance.
"Brother..." Lin Yinyin murmured as they pulled apart, her eyes shimmering. "Let's go soak in the backyard hot spring, okay? It’s been so long since we soaked alone."
Zhang Xian looked at her moist, cherry-red lips, his Adam's apple bobbing. He tapped her nose playfully. "The competition is in a few days. Be serious.
"Huh?" Lin Yinyin tilted her head. This wasn't her brother’s usual style at all.
"Since when do you care so much about winning or losing?" she blinked. "Even the championship reward shouldn't matter to a rich guy like you, right?"
"You wouldn't understand."

"By the way," Zhang Xian said, pivoting the conversation. "My opponent in three days is Song Fei, the senior sister of Cloud Breaking Peak. You took classes there for a while, didn't you? I heard you two are quite close?"
Lin Yinyin immediately went on high alert. "What? Brother, what are you planning?" She eyed him suspiciously, her gaze scanning his face for any sign of a scheme.
"Ahem. I'm just wondering... what’s she like?"
"Brother, you're too greedy!" Lin Yinyin’s face puffed up with jealous rage. "So that's it! You don't want to soak with me because you're busy trying to hook up with another female cultivator!"

She looked pained. "I’ll help you woo Master, okay? Just stop reaching your devil's claws toward everyone else! You need to keep a low profile, or the men in this sect who want to chop you up will circle the main peak three times!"
"Little girl, what are you thinking? I want to offer her some... benefits. To have her go easy on me."
"You want to cheat?!"
Lin Yinyin perked up instantly, leaning in close. "Senior Sister Song is a fifth-level Golden Core sword cultivator. Beating her fairly would be a nightmare for you..."
"But even if you win this," she whispered, "you eventually have to face Master. And Master definitely won't help you cheat."
Zhang Xian smiled mysteriously. "I have my plans. Can you put me in touch with her?"
"Fine." Lin Yinyin pouted, reluctantly pulling out her communication jade slip. "I'll send her a message. How much are you offering?"
Zhang Xian thought for a moment. He couldn't go too high, or he'd attract unwanted greed. "One hundred thousand mid-grade spirit stones."
Lin Yinyin nodded. It was a staggering sum for most. A moment after she sent the text, the jade glowed. She made a bitter face.
"Senior Sister Song scolded you." She put on a stern, righteous face to imitate her friend: "Don't even think about it! I, Song Fei, am not that kind of woman!"
Zhang Xian tapped the table. "Tell her I’ll add another hundred thousand... and I’ll throw in an Immortal Ascension Herb."
"On it!"
A short while later, the jade slip glowed again. Lin Yinyin’s eyes went wide.
"She agreed! She even asked if you want to rehearse the fight beforehand so it looks more realistic."
"Senior Sister Song is a true professional," Zhang Xian said, a satisfied smile spreading across his face.
[/author]

chapters.title: Chapter 95 I Almost Believed It Myself
paragraphs: The following evening, Lin Yinyin quietly escorted Song Fei from the mountain gate. They boarded Zhang Xian’s flying vessel, which hovered discreetly a hundred miles outside the sect’s borders.

As she stepped onto the deck, the Senior Sister of Cloud Breaking Peak couldn't mask her astonishment. "So this is a flying vessel," she murmured, her slender fingers tracing the glowing, intricate arrays carved into the railing. Her envy was palpable. "Even my Master doesn't possess such a treasure."
Zhang Xian had been waiting in the sword chamber. Seeing them enter, he offered a salute that was as elegant as it was perfectly proper. "Senior Sister Song."

He had done his homework. Song Fei possessed a rare, top-grade Metal Spirit Root. A former rogue cultivator, she was known for being cautious and meticulous. She was undeniably beautiful, yet Zhang Xian noted with a trace of surprise that the system hadn't flagged her as a Daughter of Destiny.
A pity, he thought. The system’s criteria remained a frustrating mystery.

When Song Fei looked at Zhang Xian, a flicker of guarded discomfort crossed her face. She had heard the rumors of his predatory reputation. He couldn't possibly have designs on me, could he? I must remain vigilant!

She had never understood why a girl as talented as Lin Yinyin was obsessed with a man like Zhang Xian. But as she surveyed the breathtaking luxury of the sword chamber, the logic began to click into place.
Song Fei sighed inwardly. Zhang Xian isn't just rich; he is obscenely wealthy. Only a sword cultivator with a heart of tempered steel could resist this kind of temptation.
She cleared her throat, affecting a business-like calm. "Let’s be clear. The spirit stones and the Immortal Ascension Herb..."
"Already prepared." Zhang Xian snapped his fingers. A puppet maid glided forward instantly, presenting a jade box.

Song Fei’s breath hitched as she inspected the contents. It was exactly as promised: two hundred thousand mid-grade spirit stones and an Immortal Ascension Herb capable of purifying one’s very spirit root.
"Junior Brother... I mean, Boss, shall we begin?" She swept the treasures into her storage pouch, her loyalty bought a hundred percent by the tycoon who paid the full amount upfront.
"Just 'Junior Brother Zhang' will do. Yes, let’s begin."

Song Fei nodded, her gaze turning sharp. "My opening is three inches below my left rib. Focus your attacks there. Yinyin mentioned your mastery of the Yunmiao Sword Scripture is respectable. We’ll spar using only sword techniques to sell the act."

For the next two hours, the two rehearsed every parry and strike. Song Fei’s professionalism was terrifying; she calculated the angles, the force, and the timing of their exchanges with surgical precision.
"Won't the referee notice?" Lin Yinyin asked, her voice laced with worry.

"The referee is the Head Seat of Pill Cauldron Peak. His sword path is mediocre at best," Song Fei said with a mysterious smile. "Besides, I 'sustained' internal injuries in my last match. As the fight drags on, I’ll naturally fall into a disadvantage."
"What internal injuries?" Lin Yinyin blinked. Song Fei looked like the picture of radiant health.

"These injuries..." Song Fei suddenly circulated her energy, forcing her spiritual power into a violent reversal. Her face turned paper-pale, and she let out a sharp cough, spitting a mouthful of fresh blood onto the floor. "...are very real now. That makes it safe."
Zhang Xian: "..."
This woman’s dedication to her craft was borderline psychotic.
He hurriedly offered a top-grade spirit ginseng. "Senior Sister, please... take care of yourself," he said, his voice carrying a new note of genuine respect.
Song Fei accepted it without ceremony, wiping the blood from her lip. "Don't worry. I know my limits.
On the day of the quarterfinals, Heavenly Palace Peak was a boiling cauldron of excitement.

Zhang Xian’s match had drawn a massive crowd. Its popularity was rivaled only by the bracket featuring Li Fuxi and Lin Yinyin. The area below the stage was packed with disciples practically vibrating with the hope of seeing Zhang Xian pulverized.
Even several reclusive elders had emerged to watch, including Head Seat Zhao of Cloud Breaking Peak.
"It’s finally starting!"
"Senior Sister Song is going to end that scoundrel’s career!"
"I don't know... I heard she’s still carrying a heavy injury from her last round. She’s at a serious disadvantage."
"Match begin!" the referee roared.

Song Fei struck first. Her sword cleared its sheath like a flash of winter lightning, aiming straight for Zhang Xian’s throat. Zhang Xian raised his blade horizontally, meeting her strike with a resounding clang.
"Beautiful!" cheers erupted from the stands.

The duel that followed was a masterclass. They displayed the Yunmiao Sword Scripture to its absolute perfection. Their movements flowed like a river, offense and defense transitioning with the grace of a mountain hawk.
"Holy crap! This is amazing!"
"This is what a real sword duel looks like!"
"I hate the guy, but I have to admit, Zhang Xian’s sword path is legitimate. He’s actually holding his own against a genius!"
The disciples watched, mesmerized.
"It’s just a tragedy that Senior Sister Song is injured. Look at her face—she’s getting paler by the second. Her spiritual power is flagging. This is a battle of attrition she just can't win."

However, Head Seat Zhao of Cloud Breaking Peak frowned as he watched. As a true grandmaster, he saw the subtle cracks in the performance. Song Fei’s strikes were fierce, but she was pulling her punches at every critical junction. And Zhang Xian’s defense was too perfect, as if he knew exactly where her blade would land before she did.
A fixed match! His fist clenched, but he held his tongue.
Just as the duel reached its peak, Song Fei’s momentum faltered. Her face went deathly white. "Cough!" She sprayed a mist of blood across the stone and staggered, falling to one knee.
"I... I have lost..." Her voice was a weak, trembling whisper. The tears glistening in her eyes spoke of a soul-crushing defeat. It was a flawless performance.
"Zhang Xian wins!" the referee announced.
The crowd erupted in a fury of grief and rage.
"Dammit! This is a robbery!
"That old thief just got lucky because she was hurt!"
"Senior Sister Song! You did your best! We still believe in you!"

Zhang Xian’s eye twitched. If they hadn't spent all of yesterday rehearsing, even he would have believed her. Suppressing a laugh, he offered a Spirit Recovery Pill. "Senior Sister, please, recover well."
Song Fei took the pill with a faint, tragic "thank you." She dragged her "weakened" body off the stage, her lonely, desolate silhouette moving many disciples to actual tears.
Cloud Breaking Peak, Head Seat’s Cave Abode.
Head Seat Zhao looked at his prize disciple. "Feifei, explain yourself."
Song Fei calmly wiped a non-existent trace of blood from her mouth. "Master, I simply couldn't best him."
"Bullshit! Do you think I'm blind? That was a fix!" He pointed a finger at her nose. "And that injury? You forced your own energy into reverse! You think I can't tell?!"

Song Fei went silent, realizing she couldn't fool a grandmaster. She pulled the jade box from her storage pouch and set it on the table. As the lid opened, the rich, vibrant aura of the Immortal Ascension Herb filled the room.
"Hiss—is that an Immortal Ascension Herb?!" Zhao gasped, his eyes nearly popping out of his head.
"And a mountain of spirit stones. I'm sorry, Master," Song Fei whispered, bowing her head. "I've brought shame to our peak."
To her shock, the Head Seat’s expression flipped instantly. He grabbed her shoulders, his beard trembling with excitement. "Silly girl! You need to get closer to him!"

"Look at Li Fuxi," he hissed. "Ever since she took that kid in, her cultivation has exploded. I suspect every sword in her hand is now a Spirit Treasure! Even I might not be able to beat her anymore."
"I only regret that I wasn't born a woman," he lamented. "Otherwise, I would have won Zhang Xian over myself!"
Song Fei: "???"
"Feifei, your Master has always looked out for you..."
Song Fei felt a cold shiver of dread.
"Do you think... you could find a way to get 'intimate' with Zhang Xian?" The Head Seat rubbed his hands together greedily.
Song Fei stood up and walked toward the exit without another word.
"I'm talking to you!"
"I'm going to practice my sword."
"Forget the sword! Go seduce Zhang Xian!"

She was undeniably beautiful, yet Zhang Xian noted with a trace of surprise that the system hadn't flagged her as a Daughter of Destiny.
A pity, he thought.
The system’s criteria remained a frustrating mystery.
When Song Fei looked at Zhang Xian, a flicker of guarded discomfort crossed her face.
She had heard the rumors of his predatory reputation.
He couldn't possibly have designs on me, could he?
I must remain vigilant!
She had never understood why a girl as talented as Lin Yinyin was obsessed with a man like Zhang Xian.
But as she surveyed the breathtaking luxury of the sword chamber, the logic began to click into place.
Song Fei sighed inwardly.
Zhang Xian isn't just rich; he is obscenely wealthy.
Only a sword cultivator with a heart of tempered steel could resist this kind of temptation.
She cleared her throat, affecting a business-like calm.
"Let’s be clear.
The spirit stones and the Immortal Ascension Herb..."
"Already prepared." Zhang Xian snapped his fingers.
A puppet maid glided forward instantly, presenting a jade box.
Song Fei’s breath hitched as she inspected the contents.
It was exactly as promised: two hundred thousand mid-grade spirit stones and an Immortal Ascension Herb capable of purifying one’s very spirit root.
"Junior Brother...
I mean, Boss, shall we begin?" She swept the treasures into her storage pouch, her loyalty bought a hundred percent by the tycoon who paid the full amount upfront.
"Just 'Junior Brother Zhang' will do.
Yes, let’s begin."
Song Fei nodded, her gaze turning sharp.
"My opening is three inches below my left rib.
Focus your attacks there.
Yinyin mentioned your mastery of the Yunmiao Sword Scripture is respectable.
We’ll spar using only sword techniques to sell the act."
For the next two hours, the two rehearsed every parry and strike.
Song Fei’s professionalism was terrifying; she calculated the angles, the force, and the timing of their exchanges with surgical precision.
"Won't the referee notice?" Lin Yinyin asked, her voice laced with worry.
"The referee is the Head Seat of Pill Cauldron Peak.
His sword path is mediocre at best," Song Fei said with a mysterious smile.
"Besides, I 'sustained' internal injuries in my last match.
As the fight drags on, I’ll naturally fall into a disadvantage."
"What internal injuries?" Lin Yinyin blinked.
Song Fei looked like the picture of radiant health.
"These injuries..." Song Fei suddenly circulated her energy, forcing her spiritual power into a violent reversal.
Her face turned paper-pale, and she let out a sharp cough, spitting a mouthful of fresh blood onto the floor.
"...are very real now.
That makes it safe."
Zhang Xian: "..."
This woman’s dedication to her craft was borderline psychotic.
He hurriedly offered a top-grade spirit ginseng.
"Senior Sister, please... take care of yourself," he said, his voice carrying a new note of genuine respect.
Song Fei accepted it without ceremony, wiping the blood from her lip.
"Don't worry.
I know my limits.
On the day of the quarterfinals, Heavenly Palace Peak was a boiling cauldron of excitement.
Zhang Xian’s match had drawn a massive crowd.
Its popularity was rivaled only by the bracket featuring Li Fuxi and Lin Yinyin.
The area below the stage was packed with disciples practically vibrating with the hope of seeing Zhang Xian pulverized.
Even several reclusive elders had emerged to watch, including Head Seat Zhao of Cloud Breaking Peak.
"It’s finally starting!"
"Senior Sister Song is going to end that scoundrel’s career!"
"I don't know...
I heard she’s still carrying a heavy injury from her last round.
She’s at a serious disadvantage."
"Match begin!" the referee roared.
Song Fei struck first.
Her sword cleared its sheath like a flash of winter lightning, aiming straight for Zhang Xian’s throat.
Zhang Xian raised his blade horizontally, meeting her strike with a resounding clang.
"Beautiful!" cheers erupted from the stands.
The duel that followed was a masterclass.
They displayed the Yunmiao Sword Scripture to its absolute perfection.
Their movements flowed like a river, offense and defense transitioning with the grace of a mountain hawk.
"Holy crap!
This is amazing!"
"This is what a real sword duel looks like!"
"I hate the guy, but I have to admit, Zhang Xian’s sword path is legitimate.
He’s actually holding his own against a genius!"
The disciples watched, mesmerized.
"It’s just a tragedy that Senior Sister Song is injured.
Look at her face—she’s getting paler by the second.
Her spiritual power is flagging.
This is a battle of attrition she just can't win."
However, Head Seat Zhao of Cloud Breaking Peak frowned as he watched.
As a true grandmaster, he saw the subtle cracks in the performance.
Song Fei’s strikes were fierce, but she was pulling her punches at every critical junction.
And Zhang Xian’s defense was too perfect, as if he knew exactly where her blade would land before she did.
A fixed match!
His fist clenched, but he held his tongue.
Just as the duel reached its peak, Song Fei’s momentum faltered.
Her face went deathly white.
"Cough!" She sprayed a mist of blood across the stone and staggered, falling to one knee.
I have lost..." Her voice was a weak, trembling whisper.
The tears glistening in her eyes spoke of a soul-crushing defeat.
It was a flawless performance.
"Zhang Xian wins!" the referee announced.
The crowd erupted in a fury of grief and rage.
"Dammit!
This is a robbery!
"That old thief just got lucky because she was hurt!"
"Senior Sister Song!
You did your best!
We still believe in you!"
Zhang Xian’s eye twitched.
If they hadn't spent all of yesterday rehearsing, even he would have believed her.
Suppressing a laugh, he offered a Spirit Recovery Pill.
"Senior Sister, please, recover well."
Song Fei took the pill with a faint, tragic "thank you." She dragged her "weakened" body off the stage, her lonely, desolate silhouette moving many disciples to actual tears.
Cloud Breaking Peak, Head Seat’s Cave Abode.
Head Seat Zhao looked at his prize disciple.
"Feifei, explain yourself."
Song Fei calmly wiped a non-existent trace of blood from her mouth.
"Master, I simply couldn't best him."
"Bullshit!
Do you think I'm blind?
That was a fix!" He pointed a finger at her nose.
"And that injury?
You forced your own energy into reverse!
You think I can't tell?!"
Song Fei went silent, realizing she couldn't fool a grandmaster.
She pulled the jade box from her storage pouch and set it on the table.
As the lid opened, the rich, vibrant aura of the Immortal Ascension Herb filled the room.
"Hiss—is that an Immortal Ascension Herb?!" Zhao gasped, his eyes nearly popping out of his head.
"And a mountain of spirit stones.
I'm sorry, Master," Song Fei whispered, bowing her head.
"I've brought shame to our peak."
To her shock, the Head Seat’s expression flipped instantly.
He grabbed her shoulders, his beard trembling with excitement.
"Silly girl!
You need to get closer to him!"
"Look at Li Fuxi," he hissed.
"Ever since she took that kid in, her cultivation has exploded.
I suspect every sword in her hand is now a Spirit Treasure!
Even I might not be able to beat her anymore."
"I only regret that I wasn't born a woman," he lamented.
"Otherwise, I would have won Zhang Xian over myself!"
Song Fei: "???"
"Feifei, your Master has always looked out for you..."
Song Fei felt a cold shiver of dread.
"Do you think... you could find a way to get 'intimate' with Zhang Xian?" The Head Seat rubbed his hands together greedily.
Song Fei stood up and walked toward the exit without another word.
"I'm talking to you!"
"I'm going to practice my sword."
"Forget the sword!
Go seduce Zhang Xian!"

chapters.title: Chapter 96 A Disciple Couldn’t Wish for More
paragraphs: The final streak of sword light dissolved into nothingness over the Heavenly Palace Peak arena.
"Winner of Group Wu: Li Fuxi!"
As the referee’s voice rang out, a wave of awe swept through the spectator stands.
Standing on the periphery of the crowd, Zhang Xian watched from afar as his master, Li Fuxi, sheathed her blade with valiant, effortless grace.
Opposite her, Lin Yinyin rubbed her reddened wrist, her small face scrunching up in grievance.
"If this had been a real fight for your life, you would have died a dozen times over," Li Fuxi stated calmly.
"I know," Lin Yinyin pouted, looking as if she were seconds away from tears.
"Master really doesn't know the meaning of mercy." Zhang Xian shook his head, letting out a soft chuckle.
Pushing through the bustling throng, Zhang Xian headed straight for the fourth martial arts arena.
"Look, it's that Old Thief Zhang!"
"I heard he won against Song Fei by picking up scraps. She was already heavily injured, yet he struck with full force—damn, it was brutal!"
"Why isn't he studying his next opponent? What's he doing running over here?"
The whispered insults of the disciples drifted into his ears, but Zhang Xian turned a deaf ear to them all.
He had just arrived at the ring's edge when a deafening roar of cheers erupted.
On the stage, Nangong Yao, clad in a sweeping dark robe, wielded her longsword like a striking viper. Amidst flashes of golden light, every move she made ruthlessly targeted her opponent's vitals.

Her opponent was a male cultivator with dual Earth and Fire spiritual roots. Although his cultivation was slightly inferior, his defense was watertight. Every time he parried, he condensed a reddish-yellow spiritual energy shield before him.
According to the intelligence provided by that old geezer, Nangong Yao possessed a superior-grade spiritual root and was at the seventh level of the Golden Core stage.
Her opponent also held dual superior-grade spiritual roots but was only at the fifth level.
"You got this, Martial Aunt Nangong!"
"Hold the line, Senior Brother Liu!"
"It's already been over a hundred moves, and Martial Aunt Nangong still hasn't secured the win."
"Senior Brother Liu is a once-in-a-century genius of our Yunmiao Sect; he won't lose so easily!" Some infatuated female fans cheered frantically.
Zhang Xian stood at the edge of the crowd, his gaze burning like a torch as he fixed his eyes on the two clashing figures. He quietly triggered his system.
[Nangong Yao, 50-point Daughter of Destiny. Current Favorability: 0.]
"Her score dropped. Seems she hasn't been doing too well these past few years."
Zhang Xian sneered inwardly. He remembered clearly that when they first met, this woman's destiny value was at 60 points.
While he was lost in thought, he suddenly sensed two familiar auras approaching.
Turning his head, he saw Li Fuxi and Lin Yinyin had arrived at the ringside without him noticing.
"Master, Yinyin. You made it."
Li Fuxi spoke indifferently, "We came to observe the next opponent."
Lin Yinyin, however, leaned in close and whispered, "But you, Big Brother... why aren't you watching the matches in Groups Bing and Ding? What are you doing here?"
"Shh!" Zhang Xian made a silencing gesture, turning his gaze back to the dueling platform.
The battle on stage was reaching a fever pitch.
Nangong Yao's sword techniques grew increasingly fierce, each strike accompanied by the piercing shriek of tearing air.
Although her opponent was retreating step by step, his defense remained steady. The coordination of his Earth and Fire roots produced a synergy far greater than the sum of its parts.
"Master, who do you think will win?" Lin Yinyin asked softly.
Li Fuxi kept her eyes fixed on the stage. "Within ten moves."
As if to confirm her judgment, on the eighth move, Nangong Yao's momentum shifted abruptly.
Her figure flashed like a ghost, and her longsword erupted with blinding golden light. A single thrust fractured into countless sword shadows!
Crack!
The spiritual energy shield the opponent had hastily condensed shattered like paper.
The barrage of sword light forced the male cultivator back.
Pfft!
Three beams of sword light slammed into his body. He violently spat out a mouthful of blood, tumbled off the stage, and passed out cold.
"Senior Brother Liu!"
Several disciples cried out in grief and indignation. They rushed over, frantically lifting him onto a stretcher-type artifact before hastily fleeing the scene.
"Holy shit!"
"So cruel. That blow will keep him bedridden for at least half a year." A disciple's eyelids twitched as he spoke, staring at the shocking bloodstains left on the ground.
"Winner of Group Geng: Nangong Yao!"
Nangong Yao sheathed her sword. Her gaze inadvertently swept over Li Fuxi and the others below the stage before she turned and walked away coldly.
"So powerful," Lin Yinyin sighed. "Those sword shadows... I definitely wouldn't be able to withstand them."
"The Heavenly Palace Azure Cloud Sword is one of our sect's supreme techniques. It can only be cultivated at the Golden Core stage," Li Fuxi explained calmly.
"Master, in the semifinals half a month from now, can you defeat her?" Zhang Xian suddenly asked.
"Victory is assured."
Tsk tsk. Master is as confident as ever.
Zhang Xian sighed inwardly, hoping she wouldn't crash and burn like she did during the Muling Sect incident.
However, Master was already at the peak of the sixth level of the Golden Core stage, and she possessed two Spirit Treasures. Her chances were indeed very high.
He quickly calculated the odds in his mind.
According to the tournament schedule, his potential confrontation with Nangong Yao would most likely happen in the third-place match.
As long as Master could win, and he managed to lose at just the right moment...
Bitch.
When that time comes, on the day of the third-place match, it will be the moment we settle our accounts.
The semifinals were scheduled for half a month later.
Although Li Fuxi verbally expressed full confidence, she proactively suggested returning to the flying ship to cultivate.
"Mainly because the sword chamber on the flying ship is beneficial for cultivation... and I can also guide you both along the way."
This was Li Fuxi's excuse, though her eyes darted away slightly as she spoke.
Zhang Xian was naturally happy to agree. Master's haughty yet bashful demeanor was quite adorable.
"This disciple couldn't wish for more." He bowed, unable to hide the amusement in his eyes.
Thus, the trio returned to the flying ship to cultivate.
And naturally, in the evening, they ended up in the hot springs together.
When they grew tired from practicing in the sword chamber, maids would immediately come forward to offer spiritual fruits and melons.
Knowing his master's preferences, Zhang Xian had plates of desserts and various snacks presented one after another. The two women ate with sheer delight.
They sipped on Earth-grade Green Qiao tea.
Zhang Xian had gifted them each a portion, and now his system space was overflowing with returns—more than they could ever finish.
Although Green Qiao tea wasn't as effective as the Immortal Ascension Pill in enhancing spiritual roots, it improved comprehension—a far more mysterious and difficult aptitude to raise.

Zhang Xian felt the tea's fragrance flow between his lips and teeth, a cool sensation rushing straight to his spiritual platform. Concepts that were once obscure now unraveled before him, clear as the lines on his palm.
He had long since mastered the Green Wood Nurturing Core Sutra.

Unfortunately, he had previously given this cultivation method to Liu Qingxuan under the pretext of helping her comprehend it, so he hadn't triggered a critical return from the system. It seemed the potential of that technique had reached its limit.
However, his Azure Emperor's Rejuvenation Art had improved significantly.

He had also exchanged contribution points within the sect for a copy of the Green Tide Life and Death Art. He had seen Lu Rending use it during the previous tournament; it was both offensive and defensive, truly a rare superior-grade technique among Wood-attribute methods.
With his enhanced comprehension, cultivation progressed at a terrifying speed.

The Green Tide Life and Death Art was practically self-taught. In just three days, he had already mastered most of this technique—something that would typically take ordinary cultivators months just to begin learning.
Apart from cultivation techniques, he hadn't neglected his practice of puppetry.
After advancing to the Golden Core stage—even if it was only a first-grade False Core—Zhang Xian's spiritual sense had spiked in power.
Originally, he could barely control one puppet. Now, he could simultaneously command two.
Moreover, his Earth-grade puppet was exceptionally profound, displaying a cultivation realm one level higher than his own.
"Not enough..."
Late at night, Zhang Xian stood alone on the deck of the flying ship, gazing at the star-filled sky.
To defeat Nangong Yao, this was far from sufficient.
Although that woman's destiny value had decreased, her seventh-level Golden Core cultivation and years of combat experience were not to be underestimated.
"Brother, coming for a bath?"
Lin Yinyin's message interrupted his brooding thoughts.
"Coming!!"

chapters.title: Chapter 97 I Just Wanted a Good, Clean Fight
paragraphs: For the past half-month, they hadn't set foot off the flying boat.
Mornings were for cultivating techniques. Afternoons were spent dissecting sword arts. Evenings were dedicated to quiet meditation and insight.
And at night came the highlight of the day—soaking in the hot springs, the ultimate solace for a weary body.
The half-month flew by, and in the blink of an eye, the day of the semifinals arrived.
"Are you ready?" Li Fuxi's voice drifted over.
Today, she had changed into a rare, plain white sword robe. Two Spirit Treasure longswords hung at her waist, and her long braid was combed with meticulous precision.
Zhang Xian grinned. "Master, don't go losing on me today."
"Worry about yourself!" Li Fuxi shot him a glare.
Lin Yinyin bounced out from the cabin, still dressed in her signature green-and-white disciple uniform. "Master, Big Brother, let's go!"
The trio took to the skies on their swords, streaking toward Heavenly Palace Peak.
Lin Yinyin flew in the center, her gaze darting between the two of them, her small face a picture of inner conflict.
"What's wrong?" Zhang Xian noticed her hesitation.
"I..." Lin Yinyin bit her lip. "I want to watch Master's match, but I'm also worried about you, Big Brother..."
Zhang Xian chuckled softly, steering his sword closer.

"How about this: you go watch Master's match. As soon as it ends, come find me immediately." He lowered his voice to a conspiratorial whisper. "If Master wins, just nod. If she loses... shake your head."
"Why?"
"Just do as I say." Zhang Xian reached out and ruffled her hair.
"Okay!" Lin Yinyin agreed obediently.
It seemed Master's status in her brother's heart was climbing higher and higher. He had his own match to fight, yet his mind was on hers.
Heavenly Palace Peak soon loomed into view.
Today's arena was bustling with even more fervor than usual. Disciples from every peak had arrived early to stake out spots, terrified of missing the grand event.
After the trio landed, Zhang Xian headed toward his designated arena. Along the way, the whispers of the disciples followed him like a shadow.
"Look, it's Old Demon Zhang! Damn, looks like he arrived with Inspector Fuxi and Junior Sister Yinyin."
"Too bad his opponent today is Elder Wang Yue. I doubt he'll be able to act so cocky."
"Elder Wang Yue is high in seniority and a sixth-level Golden Core cultivator. But she has a very gentle temper, so she probably won't be too heavy-handed."
"I don't care! I just want to see Old Demon Zhang lose! I even skipped Inspector Fuxi's match just to watch this scumbag get beaten!"
The arena was already a sea of people.

When Zhang Xian stepped onto the stage, a female cultivator in white robes was already waiting opposite him. She wore her hair in a refreshing single ponytail, her features delicate and beautiful. She looked no older than her early twenties.
"Wang Yue of Heavenly Palace Peak. I seek your guidance."
Zhang Xian returned the courtesy. "Zhang Xian of Spirit Sword Peak. I seek your guidance."
Strangely, after the polite exchange, neither made a move. They simply stood there, locking eyes in a silent standoff.
[Ding! Discovered 55-point Daughter of Destiny: Wang Yue.]
[Ding! Wang Yue's Favorability toward you is 20. Binding successful.]
Interesting... Zhang Xian thought.
This Elder Wang Yue was actually a Daughter of Destiny, and her initial Favorability wasn't low, either.
Meanwhile, at another arena not far away.
Li Fuxi's sword was already unsheathed, gleaming with a chilling light.
Her opponent, Nangong Yao, was equally prepared.
Years ago, when Nangong Yao and Wang Chuan were peers, the Li Fuxi standing before her had been nothing but a naive little girl. Now, Li Fuxi’s aura was no weaker than her own!
Hmph! Why?

Over the years, Nangong Yao had ventured into countless secret realms, risking life and limb in search of opportunities. How could she possibly be inferior to a silly girl who did nothing but hide on a mountain and cultivate?
Lin Yinyin stood in the front row of the spectator seats, her small hands nervously twisting the hem of her robes, her eyes fixed unblinkingly on the stage.
A mountain breeze began to rise, fluttering everyone's robes and scattering the last of the morning mist.
The semifinals had officially begun!
Back at Zhang Xian's arena.
The two combatants stood quietly, statuesque in their immobility.
The audience below began to stir with restlessness.
"Why aren't they fighting yet?"
"Is there some shady deal going on?"
Wang Yue remained cautious. She had done her homework.
The Zhang Xian before her seemed unremarkable—merely a False Core cultivator—but he was suspected to possess a Spirit Treasure for protection. She had to be careful.
Anyone who made it to the Top Four was no ordinary individual! She couldn't let his first-grade False Core cultivation fool her.
Just as Wang Yue was pondering this, she saw Zhang Xian summon a puppet identical in size to himself.
Here it comes! Her heart tightened.
Then, she watched as the puppet silently erected an earthen shield.
Wang Yue: "?"
Starting with a defensive turtle shell right off the bat?
"Martial Nephew Zhang," she called out, a trace of confusion in her clear, melodious voice. "Don't you want to make a move?"
Zhang Xian hid behind the puppet and grinned. "Martial Aunt, ladies first."
This shameless display caused an uproar among the audience below.
"He's putting on quite the act!"
"I think he's scared!"
"Elder Wang Yue! Cut him down!"
"Then I must offend."
Wang Yue formed a seal with her left hand. Three fiery vortices instantly condensed in the air, scorching gales churning the currents. The temperature of the entire arena skyrocketed!
A rain of fire poured down!
Amidst the flames, Zhang Xian calmly flicked his sleeve.
The puppet in front of him dropped to one knee, crossing its arms and raising them high. A massive rock shield unfolded with a heavy thud, covering him like a protective umbrella.
Sizzle!
The rain of fire crashed against the rock shield, evaporating into a sky full of white steam.
The moment the thick fog obscured everyone's vision, Zhang Xian fished out a pill and popped it into his mouth with practiced ease.
Sharp-eyed spectators caught the motion and immediately started jeering.
"Damn it! Popping pills right from the start?!
"Even against Elder Wang Yue, he has to rely on cheating?!"
"Old Thief Zhang! Have you no shame?!"
"Martial Nephew Zhang, you don't actually think you can win by stalling, do you?"
Wang Yue brought the sword fingers of her left hand together. Clang! A three-foot green blade unsheathed with a ringing cry!
Suddenly, another puppet charged out from Zhang Xian's flank!
Its arms sprayed bone-chilling cold currents. The air instantly froze, forming countless ice crystals that extinguished the encroaching flames.
"A Water Puppet?!"
"How many tricks does he have up his sleeve?!"
Wang Yue flicked her wrist, and red light surged along her sword's edge. A sharp sword intent pierced through the icy mist, slashing fiercely into the puppet's chest!
"Good hit!" Cheers erupted from the crowd.
Zhang Xian's fingers flew in a blur. Two Earth Spirit Talismans ignited mid-air, forming a secondary rock shield to cover the Water Puppet, blocking the residual sword energy.
At the same time, the injured puppet retreated hastily. Its chest had been pierced, revealing the intricate, complex gear arrays spinning inside.
Just as Wang Yue was about to deliver another strike to finish it off, she saw Zhang Xian produce another identical Water Puppet.
Together with the previous Earth Puppet, they stood to her left and right, blocking her path completely.
Simultaneously, Zhang Xian himself suddenly sat down cross-legged.
In his hands, a wrench, a talisman brush, and a pile of spirit-glowing components appeared out of thin air!
Clink! Clank! Clatter!
The sounds of hammering were clearly audible in the silent arena.
Tens of thousands of spectators collectively petrified.
They watched as Zhang Xian—as if no one else was around—pried open the injured puppet's chest plate and started hammering and tinkering with the internal array. He even paused to blow away some dust.
"You..." Wang Yue's sword hand trembled slightly.
Zhang Xian didn't even look up. "Martial Aunt, don't mind me. Please continue trying to break through the defensive line."
Pfft!
Someone in the audience spat out their tea.
"Am I seeing things? On-site repairs?!"
A blush of frustration rose on Wang Yue's beautiful face, her chest heaving slightly.
What was this? An infinite loop of puppets to stall her out?

"Come on! Fight me head-on!" Her sword tip pointed directly at Zhang Xian's face, her voice finally carrying a hint of suppressed anger. "Where's the momentum you used to instantly kill Martial Nephew Lu?!"
Zhang Xian looked up with an utterly sincere expression. "That secret technique has an extremely long cooldown. It can only be used once every six months."
"You!" Wang Yue was so angry her ponytail swayed.
She had originally thought she could have a good, clean, hearty battle with Zhang Xian. But now? He was only defending, refusing to attack, and stalling with puppets, talismans, and pills.
How could anyone compete like this?!
She whipped a jade bottle out from her robes and declared sharply, "I have top-grade Spirit Recovery Pills too! You can't outlast me!"
Little did she know, Zhang Xian didn't even bother looking at her.
"Martial Aunt, if you don't attack soon, I'll be done patching this one up!"

Lin Yinyin bounced out from the cabin, still dressed in her signature green-and-white disciple uniform.

The trio took to the skies on their swords, streaking toward Heavenly Palace Peak.
Lin Yinyin flew in the center, her gaze darting between the two of them, her small face a picture of inner conflict.

"I..." Lin Yinyin bit her lip.

Zhang Xian chuckled softly, steering his sword closer.

"Why?"

"Okay!" Lin Yinyin agreed obediently.
It seemed Master's status in her brother's heart was climbing higher and higher.
He had his own match to fight, yet his mind was on hers.
Heavenly Palace Peak soon loomed into view.
Today's arena was bustling with even more fervor than usual.
Disciples from every peak had arrived early to stake out spots, terrified of missing the grand event.
After the trio landed, Zhang Xian headed toward his designated arena.
Along the way, the whispers of the disciples followed him like a shadow.
"Look, it's Old Demon Zhang!
Damn, looks like he arrived with Inspector Fuxi and Junior Sister Yinyin."
"Too bad his opponent today is Elder Wang Yue.
I doubt he'll be able to act so cocky."
"Elder Wang Yue is high in seniority and a sixth-level Golden Core cultivator.
But she has a very gentle temper, so she probably won't be too heavy-handed."
"I don't care!
I just want to see Old Demon Zhang lose!
I even skipped Inspector Fuxi's match just to watch this scumbag get beaten!"
The arena was already a sea of people.
When Zhang Xian stepped onto the stage, a female cultivator in white robes was already waiting opposite him.
She wore her hair in a refreshing single ponytail, her features delicate and beautiful.
She looked no older than her early twenties.
"Wang Yue of Heavenly Palace Peak.
I seek your guidance."
Zhang Xian returned the courtesy.
"Zhang Xian of Spirit Sword Peak.

Binding successful.]

This Elder Wang Yue was actually a Daughter of Destiny, and her initial Favorability wasn't low, either.

Her opponent, Nangong Yao, was equally prepared.

Now, Li Fuxi’s aura was no weaker than her own!
Hmph!

Over the years, Nangong Yao had ventured into countless secret realms, risking life and limb in search of opportunities.
